new_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**About Us:**
Alliance Machine Systems International, LLC is a privately held company with over 35 years of history dedicated to providing corrugated box manufacturing machines and services to the changing industry. As the paperboard packaging industry's premier global supplier of productivity-enhancing process machinery and systems, we supply innovative designs, intelligent automation, and optimized workflow, coupled with highly responsive parts and service support. Our United States and Europe based engineering, manufacturing, sales and service operations provide a global support system covering the full product portfolio of Alliance, Serco, TEI, ASC, Pallmac, J&L and Tanabe machines.
 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world.
 
 
**Job Description:**
***THIS IS AN ONSITE ROLE LOCATED IN SPOKANE, WASHINGTON.***
**Job Overview:**
Alliance Machine Systems Int is seeking a Director of Manufacturing to lead manufacturing performance and operational scale across its North American production sites.
 
 
This is a considerable leadership role for an experienced manufacturing leader who understands the complexity of producing industrial automation equipment and engineered systems.
 
 
The Director of Manufacturing will be responsible for improving the connection between engineering, production, quality, supply chain, and customer delivery.
 
 
The successful candidate will lead a manufacturing environment where products may include complex electrical, mechanical, robotic and controls. The role will involve managing high-mix production, engineered-to-order or configure-to-order manufacturing, and the delivery of technically sophisticated equipment to major industrial customers.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities:**

* Lead manufacturing operations across the company’s production facilities.
* Set standards for safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, and cost.
* Improve the transfer of products and projects from engineering into manufacturing.
* Increase capacity while maintaining quality, delivery, and customer performance.
* Improve on-time delivery, lead times, throughput, and gross margin.
* Strengthen production planning, scheduling, capacity planning, and work-in-progress control.
* Manage critical components, suppliers, and long-lead materials with procurement and supply chain teams.
* Establish scalable processes for complex, high-mix, engineered-to-order automation products and systems.
* Support new product introduction and design-for-manufacture initiatives.
* Improve collaboration across sales, engineering, project management, procurement, and manufacturing.
* Lead recovery plans for delayed or strategically important projects.
* Establish clear manufacturing and performance-management KPIs.
* Develop plant managers, production managers, and operational teams.
* Support facility expansion, automation investment, capital planning, and potential upcoming new-site development.
* Partner with the executive team on manufacturing strategy, capacity, organizational design, and long-term growth.

**Requirements:**

* 12+ years’ experience in manufacturing, operations, or plant leadership within an industrial manufacturing environment.
* At least 7 years in manufacturing leadership, with direct responsibility for manufacturing performance.
* Experience within industrial automation, robotics, machinery, electrical equipment, motion control, or engineered capital equipment manufacturing.
* Direct leadership of manufacturing operations, rather than engineering or project delivery alone.
* Experience with complex, high-mix, engineered-to-order, configure-to-order, or project-based production.
* A proven record of improving delivery, quality, productivity, capacity, cost, and gross margin.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams across production, quality, planning, and supply chain.
* Strong understanding of the transition from engineering and product design into manufacturing.
* Experience leading managers and developing scalable operational structures.
* Working knowledge of ERP, MRP, production planning, scheduling, and manufacturing-performance systems.
* Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across engineering, sales, project management, supply chain, service, and executive leadership.
* Willingness to travel to US manufacturing sites, suppliers, and customers as required.

Compensation: $150,000-180,000 base salary
 
 
Benefits: Alliance offers a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability insurance, 401K with employer match, PTO, paid holidays and a bonus program.
 
 
*At Barry-Wehmiller we recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying. We know that our differences often can bring about innovation, excellence and meaningful work—therefore, people from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply to our positions. Please let us know if you require reasonable accommodations during the interview process.*
Barry-Wehmiller is an equal opportunity employer. M/F/D/V This organization uses E-Verify.
 
 
Applicants may be subject to pre-employment screening which may include drug screening, reference checks, employment verifications, background screening and/or skills assessments.
 
 
**Company:**
Alliance

new_roles.title: Director, Manufacturing Operations (Bulking) 5680
new_roles.description:
**Director, Manufacturing Operations (Bulking)**

**Direct Hire**

**Onsite - Windsor, CO**

**Position Summary**

The Director, Manufacturing Operations (Bulking) provides leadership and accountability for sterile and non-sterile bulking operations within a regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environment. This role is responsible for safe, compliant, reliable, and efficient execution of manufacturing activities, including production performance, product quality, process reliability, workforce capability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead day-to-day bulking operations across multiple products, processes, and shifts.
* Ensure production schedules are executed safely, compliantly, and efficiently while meeting business and customer commitments.
* Drive performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, capacity, yield, cycle time, right-first-time, and equipment reliability metrics.
* Establish operating standards, performance management routines, and accountability systems across the organization.
* Partner with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, MS&T, Validation, Supply Chain, and Regulatory teams to improve process performance, resolve operational challenges, and support strategic objectives.
* Provide leadership for deviations, investigations, CAPAs, change controls, audits, inspections, and regulatory compliance activities.
* Support technology transfers, process scale-up, validation, equipment qualification, automation initiatives, and implementation of new manufacturing technologies.
* Develop managers, supervisors, technical specialists, and manufacturing teams while building organizational capability and succession pipelines.
* Lead Lean, Six Sigma, standard work, and continuous improvement initiatives to improve reliability, reduce variability, and increase operational efficiency.
* Manage operating budgets, capital investments, staffing plans, and resource allocation while supporting future growth and capacity requirements.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, including aseptic processing, contamination control, and cGMP requirements.
* Ability to lead a diverse portfolio of complex manufacturing processes while establishing consistent standards across products, teams, and shifts.
* Demonstrated success leading and developing managers and frontline teams in a regulated manufacturing environment.
* Strong understanding of process control, equipment reliability, validation, technology transfer, and manufacturing scale-up.
* Ability to interpret production, quality, capacity, and financial data and translate it into clear priorities and executable plans.
* Proficiency in risk assessment, root cause analysis, deviation investigation, CAPA, and change management.
* Track record of improving safety, quality, delivery, cost, workforce capability, and operational performance through disciplined execution.
* Strong judgment and decision-making skills, including the ability to balance patient safety, compliance, supply, and business needs.
* Effective communicator with the ability to influence senior leaders, technical partners, and frontline teams and represent Manufacturing during audits and inspections.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional work with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, MS&T, Validation, Supply Chain, and Regulatory partners.
* Working knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, tiered management, standard work, or comparable continuous improvement systems.
* Strategic, hands-on, and adaptable leadership style suited to a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.

**Education & Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or another STEM discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or similarly regulated manufacturing environments, including significant production operations leadership experience.
* Significant experience in sterile or aseptic manufacturing operations required; experience with formulation, compounding, bulking, filling, or related processing strongly preferred.
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including leadership of leaders and/or multi-shift manufacturing teams.
* Demonstrated success improving operational performance, building workforce capability, and leading cross-functional change in a regulated environment.

new_roles.description:
**Job Description**
**Director Operations for Drug Product**
Do you aspire to secure a critical role in the production of biologics-based medicines? Are you excited to lead dynamic teams in a state-of-the-art facility that brings transformative biotech treatments to patients globally? We invite you to become a part of our journey as the Director Operations for Drug Product. This role offers you the chance to contribute to the site's development and wield technical leadership to ensure successful GMP manufacturing.
 
 
**Principle Roles & Responsibilities / Accountabilities**

* The Director, Operations – Drug Product plays a critical part in strategic project realization of the Wilmington Biotech facility, a new hi-potent facility in our company's Biologic manufacturing network, ensuring that site’s mission and objectives are effectively achieved, consistent with our company's requirements to ensure compliance, safety and reliable supply to our customers.
* As a key member of the Site Leadership Team, you'll have the opportunity to shape site and organizational strategies, overseeing drug product manufacturing for commercial and new product introductions.
* Be part of facility start-up to manufacture high-potent products, eg antibody drug conjugates (ADCs)
* You will work collaboratively with cross-functional teams to streamline technology transfers and commercial approvals, meanwhile nurturing and empowering your operations team.
* You'll get to foster a culture of continuous learning and improvement, leading or supporting various site functional and cross-functional structures for departmental alignment.
* Tackling resource constraints and needs, you will champion operational and technical excellence for efficient production and implement Lean principles for process optimization.
* Upholding our Manufacturing Division Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, you will manage relevant quality topics, and ensure permanent inspection readiness.
* You will oversee financial forecasts and workload for departmental cost improvements, aligning with capital and expense targets while contributing to sustainability and cost reduction initiatives.
* You will have the chance to leverage digital tools for operational efficiency and informed decision-making, keeping pace with emerging digital technologies relevant to manufacturing processes.
* You will be accountable for achieving onsite Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), monitoring and striving to improve performance metrics related to hiring, uptime, training, change controls, investigations, CAPAs, yield, volume, production cadence, operational availability, and more.

**Qualification And Experience**
**Required Experience and Skills:**

* A degree or equivalent in Engineering, Science, Technical, or other relevant fields: Bachelor’s degree + 12 years industry experience Or Masters + 10 years Or PhD + 8 years
* 6 or more years demonstrated leadership ability and experience managing, coaching, and mentoring high-performing cross function teams.
* Demonstrated experience in a biotech/vaccines/pharma manufacturing site, project, or other relevant roles, specifically drug product sterile manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing clinical and commercial products.
* Understanding of cGMP requirements for commercial high-potent ADC manufacturing of drug product

**Preferred Experience And Skills**

* Sterile manufacturing leadership & operations, with preferred multi-product experience.
* A leader who inspires, coaches, and fosters a high-performance organizational culture.
* A continuous learner who cultivates a culture of ongoing development within your team.
* An innovative thinker with excellent decision-making and problem-solving skills.
* Experienced in leading highly effective cross-functional teams with a passion for shaping the future of our organization.
* Capable of influencing and building relationships across organizational layers, as well as externally with partners.

new_roles.title: Plant Director
new_roles.description:
**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!**
Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you'll lead great people, drive meaningful impact, and help shape the future of our business while supporting the bakery and restaurant teams behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests enjoy every day. That's the kind of culture that has earned us a place on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For® list every year since 2014.

**The Plant Director**
provides strategic and operational leadership for a three-shift, seven-day manufacturing facility encompassing approximately 160 full-time, non-union employees. Leading all aspects of production and packaging operations, you will drive performance, efficiency, quality, and continuous improvement across scheduling, logistics, pre-scaling, mixing, depositing, baking, decorating, and packaging to support the Bakery's operational and business objectives.

They utilize excellent leadership, analytical, management, and technical skills, abilities, and behaviors to drive performance in key areas such as people, safety, quality, service, and cost, aligned with measurable objectives and the Company’s Mission, Vision, and Values. The Director also assists with business continuity in the absence of the VP of Operations.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **Service oriented:**
 you are a people person who is systematic and trustworthy and interacts constructively with peers or teams of various levels demonstrating strong, positive communication skills.
* **Driven by results:**
 you are conscientious and persistent about delivering timely, high-quality deliverables, and performing all job functions safely while following instructions.
* **Improvement focused:**
 you never turn off the thought “how can I do this better/faster”.
* **Pressure resistant:**
 you have ice in your veins while under pressure. Maintaining a positive outlook at work while the heat is on is never an issue for you.

**Here’s more of what you’ll get to do:**

* Maintain positive employee relations through respectful, open, and effective two-way communication at the individual and team levels.
* Partner with human resources and training departments to develop, implement, and maintain effective training and development programs that support performance goals and provide a satisfying work environment.
* Maintain a fair and professional work environment that balances business objectives with quality-of-work-life factors for employees.
* Work with Human Resources to ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and company policies, while driving improvements in employee performance as measured by turnover rate, attendance, and feedback mechanisms.
* Oversee production planning and scheduling to optimize service and efficiency, balancing resources such as crewing, materials, and equipment with other department managers.
* Supervise the development of synchronized crewing, equipment setup, and materials preparation plans to ensure schedule attainment and optimize capacity utilization.
* Manage timekeeping, labor efficiency, and plant productivity in compliance with legal and company policies, aiming to minimize overtime and control non-productive line time.
* Collaborate with the Plant Engineer to ensure preventive and emergency maintenance efforts are effective, minimizing downtime and optimizing machine performance.
* Manage material usage to ensure minimal waste and maximum yield, while maintaining strict adherence to product quality standards and inventory management.
* Monitor spending and manage operations within approved budget levels, while driving improvements in cost performance through labor productivity, waste reduction, and yield maximization.
* Ensure disciplined compliance with product and process quality standards, food safety, and regulatory requirements, striving for “EXCELLENT” or “SUPERIOR” scores in third-party audits.
* Lead plant safety efforts, including co-chairing the Safety Steering Committee, safety inspections, and training, while driving improvements in safety performance as measured by injury frequency and workers' compensation data.
* Participate in business plan development, budgeting processes, and plant-level meetings to ensure effective communication and alignment with operational goals.
* Ability to transform the facility into a CI culture driven by people, process and equipment/technology.
* Ensure the utilization of 4-step process to drive result in sustainability which are Huddles, Daily meeting, utilization of Red Zone and Sic meetings.

**What we require:**

* Minimum of 15 years of experience in food manufacturing management, preferably in the bakery/dessert industry, with demonstrated success at the Plant Manager or Director of Manufacturing/Operations level.
* Bachelor’s degree (MBA a Plus)
* Strong experience with food safety, food process equipment, and regulations.
* Strong experience with emergency preparedness and emergency response plans and procedures.
* Familiar with regulatory and safety codes, including USDA, FDA, and OSHA regulations.
* Knowledge and demonstrated skill in lean manufacturing, Kaizen, kitting, and Six Sigma techniques.
* Prior experience with direct responsibility for a large-scale P&L.
* Strong and effective strategic management skills, including long-range planning, organizing, communicating, influencing, gathering and using information, and motivating a team to achieve results. Ability to use, and teach others to use, various analytical tools and techniques.
* Demonstrated mentoring skills.

**What we offer:**

* Eligible for annual bonus
* Eligible for annual equity grants
* Medical, Dental & Vision
* Eligible for benefits first day of the month following date of hire
* 401K with company match
* 3 weeks of vacation which increases to 4 weeks starting in your 5th year
* 5 days of sick time per year (first year prorated)
* Tuition Reimbursement of $2,500 for qualified programs
* Adoption Assistance Benefit of $2,500
* 25%-35% discount when dining as a guest
* Reusable gift card loaded annually for your dining enjoyment

**About the Company:**

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery creates over 35,000 delicious cheesecakes per day across our two facilities in Calabasas, CA and Rocky Mount, NC plus other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees, and third-party bakery customers.

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery is a subsidiary of The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated. Recognized as a Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® since 2014, The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a global $3.8 billion public company with more than 370 casual dining restaurants and over 48,000 staff members.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming workplace for all. We welcome applicants from a wide variety of identities, ideas, perspectives, backgrounds and experiences to apply. The Cheesecake Factory offers reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities.

#SoCheesecake #LifeAtCheesecake

To notify of a non-compliant job posting, please send a notice to ats@thecheesecakefactory.com.

We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.
 
 
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and require your commitment and detailed attention toward safe and repeatable space flight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.
 
 
We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!
 
 
Blue Origin is scaling production of its electric propulsion systems. We are hiring a Director to own the manufacturing outcome for that product line and to carry it from development hardware into rate production.
 
 
You will be the single-threaded leader for Operations of this program: one person accountable for rate, quality, cost, and people, with full authority over the entire in-program production flow.
 
 
This is a build-it role, not a run-it role. You will define the value streams, stand up integration with support organizations, and build the team that runs the line — working concurrently with an active design program rather than behind a frozen one.
 
 
**Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To**

* Own the strategy, roadmap, and priorities for successful manufacturing outcomes of the electric propulsion thruster line — delivery rate, quality, cost, and the people who produce it.
* Build the production organization. Define the value streams, stand up production control and manufacturing engineering, and hire and develop the leadership beneath you as the program scales.
* Own the get-to-rate plan. Define the path from development build to sustained rate production, and demonstrate cycle time at the rate-readiness gate as a committed acceptance number rather than a projection.
* Lead the transition from development build into rate production, including the qualification of tooling, processes, and work instructions required to produce repeatably at rate.
* Drive producibility into the product during design, rather than absorbing it on the floor later. Own the manufacturing view of the bill of materials as the product configuration evolves.
* Establish and own the program's working interfaces with quality, supply chain, material planning, and test operations.
* Build and manage the program's manufacturing operating budget and capital plan, owning responsibility for product delivery at cost and rate.
* Set the safety and quality culture for a new production team, and hold it as the organization grows.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in an engineering or technical discipline.
* 12+ years of experience in manufacturing, production, supply chain, or operations, including 5+ years leading manufacturing organizations.
* Direct, hands-on experience taking a new product or production line from development into rate production.
* Experience carrying a product through a production-readiness or rate-readiness gate, and owning the cycle-time and capability evidence presented at it.
* Experience building an organization — defining structure, hiring leaders, and developing a team through significant growth.
* Line management of both salaried professionals and craft or technician populations.
* Demonstrated ability to operate in ambiguity: making defensible assumptions and moving forward on an incomplete definition, then correcting as information arrives.
* Ability to travel frequently, up to approximately 35%, to other Blue Origin sites.
* Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 15+ years of manufacturing and operations experience.
* Propulsion, spacecraft, satellite, or other high-reliability low-volume hardware experience.
* Experience transitioning a product from low-volume, high-mix build into repeatable rate production.
* Demonstrated cycle-time or throughput improvement with measured results.
* Experience standing up production at a new or greenfield manufacturing site.
* Experience managing a build against a bill of materials that changed materially during production ramp.
* Formal lean or continuous-improvement training, with applied results on a production line.
* Master’s degree in engineering or technical field, or MBA.

* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)

new_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Quality
new_roles.description:
At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.
 
 
For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.
 
 
At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.
 
 
We are looking for a S
**r. Manager, Quality**
to join our team in one of today’s most exciting technologies. This role will report to
**Director of Quality**
and based in
**Newark, Delaware. This is a fully on-site, in office role 5 days a week**
.
 
 
**Role and Responsibilities:**

* Ensure 100% Quality assurance at the Skid line manufacturing through inspection, testing, and sub-component testing/inspection. Assist in hiring personnel needed to support this effort.
* Partner with Install Quality team (field) to understand real time (daily) what items are escaping the plant and instituting immediate mitigation plans including addressing any inventory in the pipeline not yet installed.
* Implement permanent corrective actions working with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply chain, or SQE as per relevance on each issue.
* Provide quality input into the new equipment being purchased for the scaling of Delaware manufacturing. Include inputs for quality assurance into equipment design, and verification of process steps. Understand and provide input into the planned operation, what can be bypassed, maintenance plans, calibration or drift of the equipment, automation that can fail and be undetected leading to quality escapes.
* Participate and understand results from testing in the plant; Functional test, Tommy test, FIT, etc. Drive pareto of failures to help cross functional problem solving of test failures.
* Implement a 100% functional test (new) on skid final product assembly; electrical continuity, communications integrity, piping assurance, start up simulation, etc. to assure 100% QA prior to shipping to customer.
* Ensure skid components and systems have latest FW revision prior to shipping to the W/H, or out of W/H to field.
* Work with CIG and Manufacturing Engr, and NPI to implement workload being removed from the customer install side and being moved into skid assembly. Provide oversight to ensure best quality achievement; ensure work instructions are clear, operators trained, workstations have proper tools, and judgement criteria.
* Collaborate with Supplier Quality / Suppliers to achieve zero-defect flow (“dock-to-stock”) for all purchased, contract manufacture parts, materials, and Bloom Energy manufactured parts.
* Drive component and design failures back to the earliest point of detection in the process.
* Ensure manufacturing process have Control plans with CTQ, and POA built in to each station.
* Work collaboratively with Design teams to DFM, through a “registration system”, and Pokeyoke assembly methods for highest quality assurance.
* Drive test excellence in the manufacturing plan to ensure that equipment and test stations are certified with robust qualification programs, that are documented and controlled for changes with proper accuracy and gage R&R techniques.
* Drive yield task forces to achieve company wide targets at each manufacturing point under this scope, with cross functional teams driving top pareto issues to RCCA.
* Ensure early engagement with the product engineering team to teach and perform early stage risk assessments (DFMEA et.al.)
* Design for manufacturability and reliability improvements during the early design stages of product development.
* Work with Engineering NPI and the manufacturing engineering teams to perform PFMEA, write work instructions, and establish quality check-points to guarantee zero-defect quality in production.
* Develop and implement formal, comprehensive process documentation including process flow diagrams, Process FMEAs, process control plans, operations method Sheets, manufacturing quality charts (MQCs) and etc.
* Lead critical problem solving task forces with emphasis on cross functional inputs, accountability, time to RCCA, and ensurance of mitigation of inventory, or field units at risk.
* Troubleshoot product issues by reviewing engineering drawings and design requirements. Drive a rigorous resolution process for product quality, reliability and design issues.
* Perform data-driven root cause failure analyses for design, manufacturing, and administrative problems.
* Perform process audits to monitor, continuously improve, and sustain superior product quality.
* Demonstrate the ability to interface and work collaboratively across departments internally and with suppliers and customers, (including Purchasing, Quality, R&D, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, Marketing and Finance), while building strong and cooperative working relationships.
* Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Establish and govern site COPQ metrics (scrap, rework, sorting, and warranty risk); lead cross-functional yield-improvement blitzes targeting measurable cost reductions and scrap minimization.
* Process Capability & Zero-Defect Mentality: Drive process capability (C\_p / C\_{pk} \ge 1.33) across critical-to-quality (CTQ) operations (welding, brazing, ceramic stack assembly, plumbing/gas-delivery, and electrical integration).

**Skills and Experience:**

* More than 10 years of increasing responsibility in the areas of Quality, and Manufacturing .
* Experience implementing company-wide ISO 9001 procedures and TS16949 standards and related process documentation. Possess working knowledge of process capability and control requirements, methods and systems.
* Demonstrated track record of building, restructuring, or significantly scaling a manufacturing quality team during rapid production ramp-up
* Proven successful application of multi-discipline engineering problem solving techniques.
* Understand the critical elements of modern Manufacturing Statistical Process Control, (e.g., practical working knowledge and experience with SPC, Process Capability, Cp, Cpk, etc.)
* Understand the critical elements of modern Reliability Engineering, (e.g., MCF, MTBF, MTT, etc.)
* Certification in a recognized problem-solving methodology such as six-sigma Black Belt, 8D, or Global Problem Solving.
* Strong verbal/active listening/written communications.
* Demonstrate planning and leadership skills.
* Expert with metrology, calibration, and Gage R & R’s.
* Ability to train in Quality System Auditing.
* Fluent in product phase-gate, NPI and technology transfer.
* Expertise in applying PPAP, First Article Inspections (FAI) and Reports).
* Strong critical thinking, analytical skills, and problem solving.
* Ability to effectively work within a very intense, dynamic, fast-paced, and demanding work environment.
* Familiarity with industry codes and quality standards applicable to clean power systems (ISO 9001:2015 required; working knowledge of ASME, NFPA, or UL standards preferred).
* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality / Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) and ASQ Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE) alongside CQE and Six Sigma Black Belt.
* Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office Suite and statistical software.
* Possess a passion for excellence.
* Unrestricted willingness to travel to all regions. Travel may be up to 25% of time.
* BS, MS or PhD in Mechanical/Material Science/Chemical/Electrical/Systems Engineering.
* Direct experience managing high-temperature fluidics/gas delivery, welding/brazing, ceramic integration, power electronics, or structural enclosures is a strong plus.

Bloom Energy is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions on the basis of merit. We are committed to compliance with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants, will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability. Bloom Energy makes reasonable accommodations, consistent with applicable laws, for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified applicant or employee with a disability, who can perform the essential job functions, unless undue hardship would result.
 
 
At Bloom Energy, we are committed to supporting the well-being of our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits package for eligible employees includes competitive Medical, Dental, and Vision plans with a large employer contribution, a 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match, generous Mental Health Support services, Legal services, virtual Physical Therapy access, and Fertility & Family Forming benefits.
 
 
Bloom Energy is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The total compensation for this position includes standard company benefits and is based on various factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience.
 
 
Salary Ranges:
 
 
$149,300.00 - $214,700.00

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Regional Food Safety Quality Assurance (FSQA)
new_roles.description:
**Purpose**
Dole Packaged Foods is a purpose led organization that is a champion of accessible fruit nutrition and builds a brighter future for people through the goodness of fruit.
 
 
At Dole, our culture is uniquely driven by core Values. Our commitment to these Values transforms our work into a meaningful journey toward a brighter future together. Here, you'll be part of a respectful, inclusive culture that deeply values our colleagues, customers, and global communities. We strive for excellence, empowering each other to confidently overcome challenges, continuously learn, and achieve world-class results. Guided by unwavering integrity, our actions consistently reflect our commitment to always doing what's right, fostering lasting trust and strong relationships. Through a spirit of collaboration, we cultivate positivity, generosity, and genuine teamwork, enabling collective success toward our One Dole Purpose. Our innovative spirit leads directly to meaningful outcomes and business success.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Regional Food Safety & Quality Assurance (FSQA) provides leadership and direction for food safety and quality across the North America region. Serving as a key partner to regional business and Supply Chain leadership, this role oversees regional and site FSQA execution, drives performance and continuous improvement, and serves as a primary Quality representative for customers and key business partners.
 
 
Working collaboratively across Operations, Supply Chain and Global FSQR, the Senior Manager helps translate company priorities into effective execution while strengthening food safety and quality capability throughout the region. This is a highly visible leadership role for an experienced professional who enjoys developing people, solving complex problems and influencing how Quality supports the business.
 
 
This role provides flexibility to work in a hybrid environment of home and our Westlake Village, CA office. (Hybrid is defined as 3 times per week in the office).
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**Primary Accountabilities:**
**Regional FSQA Leadership & Execution**

* Lead food safety and quality execution across North America, providing oversight to regional and site FSQA teams and serving as the primary FSQA partner to regional business and Supply Chain leadership.
* Monitor significant food safety and quality risks, performance gaps and corrective actions, ensuring effective execution, follow-through and appropriate escalation.
* Lead, coach and develop FSQA personnel while strengthening food safety and quality culture, capability and accountability across the region.

**Program Deployment & Capability Building**

* Lead regional implementation and reinforcement of company food safety and quality programs, standards and requirements including training and capability building across applicable functions.
* Coordinate regional food safety and quality incidents, ensuring appropriate assessment, communication, escalation and corrective action in partnership with relevant stakeholders.
* Partner with Global FSQR subject-matter experts to address technical and capability needs and support development of regional or facility SOPs, protocols and other supporting documentation.

**Customer, Business & Supply Chain Partnership**

* Serve as the primary North America Quality Representative for customers including strategic customer relationships, audits, inquiries and quality-related issues.
* Partner with Supply Chain, Operations, Commercial, Procurement, R&D and other functions to integrate food safety and quality requirements into business activities, commercialization and change initiatives.
* Coordinate regional FSQA activities involving suppliers, third-party manufacturers, warehousing and transportation in partnership with the appropriate Global FSQR teams.

**Performance & Continuous Improvement**

* Drive regional FSQA performance through KPIs, scorecards, trend analysis and management reporting, providing appropriate visibility to regional leadership and Global FSQR.
* Identify systemic risks, recurring issues and improvement opportunities and drive effective corrective and preventive actions across the region.
* Manage regional FSQA resources and priorities to support business needs, strengthen execution and continuously improve food safety and quality performance.
* Other duties as assigned

**Qualifications**
**Experience, Knowledge, & Skills You Bring:**

* 8+ years of progressive experience in food safety, quality assurance or related food manufacturing disciplines, including demonstrated leadership responsibility.
* Strong knowledge of food safety and quality management systems, HACCP/Preventive Controls, GMPs, GFSI-recognized certification schemes and applicable U.S./Canada food regulations.
* Experience working across manufacturing, Supply Chain and cross-functional business environments.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence and work effectively across organizational boundaries.
* Experience managing customer quality relationships and communicating effectively with senior business leaders.
* Strong understanding of incident management, risk assessment, corrective and preventive action, and continuous improvement principles.
* Strong analytical and communication skills with the ability to translate technical issues and performance data into practical business actions.
* Demonstrated ability to coach and develop technical professionals and build effective cross-functional relationships.

**What You’ll Need to Succeed:**

* Passionate about a purpose driven career
* Committed to fostering inclusive environments that support employee development and well-being
* Sets clear expectations, encourages innovation, and drives continuous improvement
* Models and coaches towards transparency and integrity in decision-making
* Effectively facilitates cross-team communication and teamwork

**Education & Certification:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Biology, Chemistry or Life Sciences is required.
* Advanced degree preferred but not required.
* HACCP and/or Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (PCQI) training strongly preferred.
* Relevant GFSI, auditing, food safety or quality certifications are beneficial.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to sit and use the computer for extended periods of time; ability to answer phones and use a variety of office equipment; ability to lift 15 pounds and reach overhead.

**Travel Requirements:**

* Approximately 30-40%, including travel to company facilities, customers, and business partners as required.

**All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.**
**For Jobs Based In California**
Hiring Pay Scale: $145,000 to $170,000
 
 
Dole Packaged Foods is committed to paying our Associates fairly and equitably. The pay rate offered will consider a wide range of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, accomplishments, and location. Pay scales are subject to review on a regular basis and will be updated as appropriate.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality Assurance - GxP (GCP)
new_roles.description:
PTC Therapeutics is a global commercial biopharmaceutical company. For over 25 years our team has been deeply committed to a unified purpose: Extending life’s moments for children and adults living with a rare disease.
 
 
At PTC, we cultivate an inclusive culture where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds to join our team
**,**
fostering a strong sense of belonging.
 
 
Visit our website to learn more about our company and culture!
 
 
Site: www.ptcbio.com
 
 
**Job Description Summary**
The Senior Manager, Quality Assurance - GxP (GCP) is responsible for managing GxP Quality Assurance (QA) functions with an emphasis on Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance for development products. This involves engaging and collaborating with cross-functional internal and external teams to evaluate processes, procedures, and activities for adherence to relevant industry standards, regulatory guidelines, and company Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) as appropriate.
 
 
The incumbent will support and/or conduct internal and external GCP audits of investigator sites, vendors, clinical study reports, investigator brochures, and submission documents, etc.
 
 
She/He will assist in inspection readiness activities.
 
 
She/He may manage direct reports.
 
 
The incumbent works cross-functionally with internal departments and external resources on GxP QA related issues.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Quality Assurance – GxP (GCP)supports adherence to relevant regulatory requirements and company Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) as appropriate.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**Job Description:**

* Partners with Clinical Development/Operations and actively participates in clinical study teams to ensure GCP compliance. Assists in identifying and communicating clinical trial-related risks and opportunities for process improvement. Reviews study-related documents and plans.
* Performs internal and external audits as assigned to ensure compliance with GXP regulations and guidelines.
* Communicates audit results to internal stakeholders and writes audit report.
* Assesses audit responses and ensures closure of corrective action preventative actions (CAPAs).
* Leads backroom activities during regulatory authority inspections and assists with GxP inspection readiness activities.
* Supports Quality Management System (QMS) including, but not be limited to, the following activities:
* QA review/approval of deviations, CAPAs and change controls.
* Drafts, reviews, and approves SOPs.
* May manage, coach, and mentor direct reports.
* Performs other tasks and assignments as needed and specified by management.

**Qualifications**
Bachelor’s degree in a scientific discipline and a minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in Quality Assurance or related role in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or related environment.
 
 

* Detailed knowledge and understanding of GCP regulations.
* Demonstrated experience leading and/or conducting QA audits.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing risk-based audit plans.
* Demonstrated ability to develop and foster positive, collaborative relationships with internal staff as well as with external, third-party vendors.
* Demonstrated leadership ability and experience managing, coaching, and mentoring direct reports.
* Experience supporting regulatory agency inspections.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively, as required, in a fast-paced, matrixed, team environment consisting of internal and external team members.
* Analytical thinker with excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines.
* Excellent planning, organization, and time management skills including the ability to support and prioritize multiple projects.

**Special Knowledge Or Skills And/or Licenses Or Certificates Preferred.**

* Experience writing and reviewing SOPs.
* Clinical lab experience.
* Registered GxP Quality Assurance Certifications.
* Experience supporting regulatory agency (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA) inspections.
* Knowledge and experience in Good Laboratory Practice (GLP), Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), and/or Good Pharmacovigilance Practice (GVP) regulations.

*Travel requirements: Up to 30% (Domestic and International)*
*Expected Base Salary Range: $141,900 -$175,000. The base salary offered will be contingent on assessment of candidate education level, background, and experience relative to the requirements of the position they are being considered for, as well as review of internal equity.*
*In addition to base salary, PTC employees are also eligible for short- and long-term incentives. All eligible employees may also enroll in PTC’s medical, dental, vision, and retirement savings plans*
**EEO Statement**
**PTC Therapeutics is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all individuals, regardless of race, color, national origin, gender, age, physical characteristics, social origin, disability, religion, family status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability, veteran status or any unlawful criterion under applicable law. We are committed to treating all applicants fairly and avoiding discrimination.**

new_roles.description:
**POSITION DETAILS**
Job Title: Senior Manager, Quality Assurance, Regulatory & Compliance
 
 
Location: Yonkers, NY (Hybrid or Remote w/ Travel)
 
 
Reports To: Sr. Director, Supply Chain
 
 
Compensation: $120,000 to $130,000
 
 
**About The Role**
We are seeking an experienced and highly analytical
**Senior Manager, Quality Assurance, Regulatory & Compliance**
to lead our global quality and compliance functions. As a rapidly growing hair care brand, we require a hands-on leader to ensure our products meet the highest standards of safety, efficacy, and legal compliance across all global markets.
 
 
In this role, you will own the end-to-end quality control lifecycle, from raw material qualification to finished goods distribution, while serving as our internal subject matter expert for global cosmetic regulations. You will play a critical role in managing our compliance with the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act (MoCRA) in the US, as well as maintaining active registrations and compliance in the EU, UK, and other international markets.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
**Global Regulatory Compliance**

* MoCRA & FDA Leadership: Serve as the designated "Responsible Person" (or primary liaison) to ensure full compliance with MoCRA requirements, including facility registrations, product listings, safety substantiation, and fragrance allergen disclosures.
* International Market Registrations: Lead and maintain product registrations across global portals, including the EU Cosmetic Products Notification Portal (CPNP), UK Submit Cosmetic Product Notification (SCPN), and Health Canada.
* Claims Substantiation & Labeling: Serve as the definitive regulatory authority for product marketing and packaging. Collaborate with Marketing, Legal, and Product Development to ensure all packaging artwork, ingredient lists (INCI), and warnings comply strictly with FDA and international standards. Maintain ownership of the testing matrix and claims substantiation repository, establishing a mandatory QA/Regulatory approval gate for all technical data prior to market release.
* Adverse Event Management: Oversee the adverse event reporting system; manage serious adverse event reporting timelines, maintain recordkeeping, and ensure root-cause investigations are conducted.
* Regulatory Intelligence: Monitor shifting regulatory landscapes (e.g., Prop 65, volatile organic compounds (VOC) restrictions for aerosols, state-level bans) and proactively update internal formulations and policies to mitigate risk.

**End-to-End Quality Control & Assurance**

* CMO & Supplier Management: Audit, qualify, and manage third-party contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs), raw material suppliers, and packaging vendors. Ensure alignment with GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices) and ISO 22716 standards.
* Product Testing & Release: Oversee stability, compatibility, and microbiological testing protocols for new and existing hair care formulations. Review and approve Certificates of Analysis (COAs), batch records, and retain samples
* Packaging Compatibility & Structural Testing: Lead Package Compatibility Testing (PCT), E&L studies, and structural assessments (e.g., torque, seal, barrier). Ensure all packaging meets ISTA transit standards and maintains integrity with complex hair care formulations like aerosols and surfactants.
* Issue Resolution: Lead root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and Out of Specification (OOS) investigations. Make critical disposition decisions regarding product approvals, quarantines, or rejections.
* Quality Management Systems (QMS): Build, scale, and maintain internal QMS documentation, including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), finished product specifications, and quality agreements with external partners.

**Cross-Functional Leadership**

* New Product Development (NPD): Act as the regulatory and quality gatekeeper during the R&D and commercialization phases. Advise on ingredient restrictions and formulation safety.
* Team Development: Manage and mentor quality coordinators or specialists. Provide training to cross-functional teams (Operations, Customer Service) on regulatory requirements and quality standards.

**Required Qualifications**

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biology, Regulatory Affairs, or a related scientific discipline. Master’s degree preferred.
* Experience: 7–10+ years of progressive experience in Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs within the CPG industry, specifically in cosmetics, personal care, or hair care.
* Regulatory Expertise: Deep, demonstrated understanding of US FDA cosmetic regulations (MoCRA), EU CosReg, UK regulations, and global compliance frameworks.
* Quality Systems: Strong background in cGMP, ISO standards (e.g., ISO 22716), ISTA transit testing, and handling FDA inspections or third-party audits.
* Hair Care Knowledge: Familiarity with hair care specific formulation challenges, including emulsions, surfactants, aerosols (VOC compliance), and clinical testing for hair claims.
* Skills: Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional communication skills. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and balance risk-management with commercial business goals.

**Preferred Experience**

* eQMS Implementation: Proven experience selecting, implementing, or migrating electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) such as MasterControl, Veeva, or TrackWise, as well as integrating quality modules within ERPs like NetSuite or SAP.
* Advanced Formulation Expertise: Direct experience managing compliance and quality control for Over-the-Counter (OTC) monographs (e.g., dandruff shampoos, minoxidil hair growth treatments), continuous mist aerosols, or professional-grade salon chemical treatments.
* Retailer & Clean Beauty Standards: Deep understanding of specialized retailer compliance frameworks, such as "Clean at Sephora," Target Clean, or Credo Beauty guidelines, and experience managing the formulation and documentation required to meet them.
* Professional Certifications: Active Regulatory Affairs Certification (RAC) or American Society for Quality (ASQ) certifications, such as Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Manager of Quality (CMQ/OE).
* Sustainability & ESG: Experience guiding quality and regulatory practices for sustainability initiatives, such as achieving B-Corp certification, managing PCR material tracking, or navigating extended producer responsibility (EPR) packaging laws.

**SCOPE OF DECISION-MAKING**
**Autonomous Decisions (Direct Authority)**

* Product Disposition: Final authority to release, quarantine, or reject finished goods and raw materials based on test results, COAs, and quality standards.
* Compliance Sign-Off: Sole approval authority on ingredient lists (INCI), regulatory packaging warnings, and safety substantiation prior to printing or market launch.
* Supplier Qualification: Authority to approve, conditionally approve, or disqualify contract manufacturers (CMOs), packaging vendors, and raw material suppliers based on audit results and cGMP compliance.
* CAPA & Investigations: Direct control over resolving Out of Specification (OOS) investigations, determining root causes, and enforcing Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) with internal teams and external vendors.
* SOP Enforcement: Authority to implement, update, and enforce Quality Management System (QMS) policies and standard operating procedures across the organization.

**Collaborative & Escalated Decisions (Advisory Role)**

* Product Recalls & Withdrawals: Lead the initial risk assessment and data gathering for potential safety issues, but escalate final recall execution and communication strategies to Executive Leadership and Legal.
* New Market Entry: Advise the Executive team on the regulatory feasibility, costs, and timeline of entering new international markets (e.g., reformulations needed, registration hurdles).
* Marketing Claims: Partner with Legal and Marketing to negotiate and finalize high-risk product claims (e.g., "clinically proven," "hair growth"), balancing commercial goals with regulatory constraints.
* Major Capital Expenditures: Recommend investments in enterprise quality software (eQMS) or third-party laboratory partnerships for executive budget approval.

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Title: Senior Manager Quality Sterility Assurance**
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
**Division/Site Specific Information**
Role reports to the Ridgefield, NJ site and reports to the Drug Product Division within the Pharma Services Group.
 
 
**Discover Impactful Work:**
As a Senior Manager of Quality at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you will guide strategic quality initiatives and support a culture of continuous improvement across our organization. You'll oversee quality management systems, ensure regulatory compliance, and enhance customer experience through excellent quality standards. Working closely with cross-functional teams, you'll develop and implement quality strategies that support our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.
 
 
A Day in the Life:
 
 

* In this role, you'll manage quality assurance and quality control teams while building strong partnerships with operations, R&D, commercial teams, and customers.
* You'll guide process improvements through Practical Process Improvement (PPI) methodologies and risk-based approaches.
* Your leadership will be essential in maintaining inspection readiness, managing customer relationships, and ensuring compliance with global regulatory requirements.
* As a member of the Quality Leadership Team, you'll support quality initiatives that deliver consistent product excellence while meeting business objectives.
* You'll develop quality professionals, lead investigations, and implement data-driven solutions that enhance our quality systems and customer satisfaction.

**Keys to Success:**
**Education/Experience**

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in pharmaceutical, medical device, or regulated life sciences industry required.
* Preferred Fields of Study: Science, Engineering, Chemistry, or related technical field
* Professional certifications desired (ASQ, Lean Six Sigma, etc.)
* 5+ years of quality management/leadership experience
* Experience hosting regulatory inspections and customer audits
* Experience implementing continuous improvement initiatives
* Experience with quality tools including FMEA, Risk Analysis, and Root Cause Analysis

**Knowledge, Skills, Abilities**

* Expert knowledge of global quality standards (ISO 13485, ISO 9001, FDA 21 CFR 820, EU MDR/IVDR)
* Strong understanding of quality management systems and GMP requirements
* Demonstrated experience leading quality investigations, CAPA, and change control processes
* Excellent project management and cross-functional leadership abilities
* Strong data analysis and problem-solving capabilities
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Ability to build collaborative relationships at all levels
* Proficiency with quality management software systems

**Benefits**
We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.
 
 
**Compensation And Benefits**
The salary range estimated for this position based in New Jersey is $143,200.00–$214,900.00.
 
 
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
 
 

* A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
* Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
* At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
* Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
* Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

new_roles.title: Director of Product Development & Industrialization
new_roles.description:
At Horizon Hobby, we inspire dreams and help build memories! Our company is the leader in the global Radio Control industry, celebrating 40 years in 2025! We offer tremendous opportunities for growth and development and a full array of benefits including discounts on our products! We are currently hiring for a Director of Product Development and Industrialization at our Pro-Line office in Banning CA!
 
 
*This is a full time, on-site position at our Pro-Line facility in Banning California. Workings hours will be Monday-Friday 8am-5pm PST.*
**Typical pay for this position is $105,000-$125,000. The final offer for this position will be based on the unique experience and qualifications of the candidate selected. This position may also be eligible for a bonus not included in the base pay range.**
The Director of Product Development & Industrialization will provide strategic leadership for the development, commercialization, and industrialization of proprietary hobby products from concept through production. This role will be leading our Product Development, Product Engineering, and Industrialization resources while overseeing the systems, processes, tooling, molds, manufacturing equipment, and technical capabilities required to deliver innovative, high-quality products to market.
 
 
This role will partner closely with Brand, Sales, Marketing, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Finance, Tooling, and external partners to identify market opportunities, translate customer needs into successful products, and ensure products are designed, developed, and launched efficiently. The role balances technical excellence with business performance, ensuring product investments align with growth objectives, customer demand, profitability targets, and long-term strategic priorities.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
Product Innovation & Strategy
 
 

* Partner with Brand and cross-functional teams to define product roadmaps, priorities, resources, and timelines.
* Drive innovation and development investments that strengthen market position, customer satisfaction, growth, and return on investment.
* Identify and prioritize new product opportunities using customer insight, competitive analysis, market trends, and commercial potential.

Product Development Leadership
 
 

* Lead and develop Product Development, Product Engineering, and Industrialization teams supporting proprietary products.
* Own product development from concept and engineering through validation, launch, and lifecycle management.
* Strengthen quality, scalability, execution, and organizational capability through standards, coaching, succession planning, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Business & Commercial Leadership
 
 

* Monitor portfolio performance and align cross-functional priorities to achieve revenue, profitability, and strategic objectives.
* Contribute to portfolio planning, market expansion, long-range growth, budgeting, forecasting, and resource allocation.
* Provide senior leadership with business reviews, development updates, performance metrics, and recommendations.

Industrialization & Manufacturing Readiness
 
 

* Lead new-product industrialization from concept through launch, applying DFM and DFA to optimize quality, scalability, cost, and manufacturing readiness.
* Partner across Engineering, Manufacturing, Tool Room, suppliers, and development teams to resolve challenges and improve processes, tooling, and capacity.
* Track launch, readiness, quality, and productivity performance to drive continuous improvement.

Tooling, Equipment & Technology
 
 

* Define requirements and roadmaps for molds, tooling, fixtures, machinery, automation, and manufacturing technology.
* Lead capital planning and business cases that improve capability, productivity, quality, cost, and return on investment.
* Manage external tooling and manufacturing partners, strengthen internal capabilities, and maintain effective engineering data and technical documentation processes.

Supplier & Partner Management
 
 

* Build strategic relationships with domestic and international manufacturing, tooling, engineering, and supplier partners.
* Evaluate supplier capabilities and performance to improve quality, speed, cost competitiveness, and alignment with business objectives.

*Success in this role requires strong leadership across innovation, engineering, manufacturing, and business functions to continuously improve speed to market, product quality, operational performance, and return on investment*
**Required**
**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering, Product Development, or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience in product management, category management, business management, product development, or a related leadership role.
* 5+ years of experience leading and developing teams.
* Demonstrated success growing a product category, business unit, or consumer product portfolio.
* Experience developing and launching successful products from concept through commercialization.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets, forecasting, business cases, and profitability.
* Proven ability to develop business strategies and translate them into measurable results.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
* Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities.
* Ability to travel as required for customer visits, product testing, trade shows, industry events, and supplier meetings.

**Preferred**

* Experience in the RC, hobby products, powersports, automotive aftermarket, consumer products, or related industries.
* Experience working directly with enthusiast communities, racers, influencers, or brand ambassadors.
* Familiarity with manufacturing processes, new product introduction, and global sourcing environments.
* Experience using product lifecycle management (PLM) and project management systems.

**Physical Requirements**

* Occasional lifting of office supplies and materials, up to 20 pounds.
* Ability to sit or stand for extended periods while working on a computer.

*The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.*
**Benefits & Other Perks**

* Medical, Dental, Vision
* HSA and FSA options
* Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Insurance
* Life Insurance and Supplemental Life Insurance
* 401(k) with a company match
* Paid Time Off
* Paid Holidays
* Internal Rewards
* Discounts on Products
* Additional Coverage such as accident, critical, hospital and pet insurance

*Horizon Hobby is a progressive, innovative company and, as such, is constantly reevaluating and reinventing the processes and procedures associated with each job. The essential duties and responsibilities of this position may change at any time. In addition, employees may be asked to work on special projects or to assist with other work necessary or important to the operation of Horizon. Your cooperation and assistance in performing such additional work is expected and appreciated.*
**Horizon Hobby, LLC is an equal opportunity and E-Verify employer**

new_roles.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
new_roles.description:
**Job Description**
The Director, Continuous Improvement leads the Supply Chain-wide capability for identifying, prioritizing, enabling, and sustaining improvements that increase business performance and organizational effectiveness across functions and end-to-end processes. This role establishes a culture of continuous improvement, advances operational and business process excellence, and enables measurable improvements in productivity, cost, quality, service, and capacity.
 
 
Working closely with cross-functional Supply Chain leaders, this position standardizes processes, uses data and insights to prioritize opportunities, and implements sustainable solutions aligned with strategic objectives. The Director maintains a strong connection to frontline operations by working directly in Supply Chain Centers and other functional environments to understand processes firsthand and translate observations into meaningful improvements.
 
 
**What You’ll Do**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive Continuous Improvement strategy and multi-year roadmap aligned with Supply Chain priorities, and advise Supply Chain leadership on opportunities that improve productivity, efficiency, cost, service, quality, capacity, and organizational effectiveness.
* Lead the deployment of consistent Continuous Improvement methodologies, tools, governance, performance expectations, and resource prioritization across Supply Chain functions.
* Work directly with Supply Chain Centers and functional teams to observe work at the point of execution, identify process variation and non-value-added activities, and implement standardized processes, operating practices, management systems, standard work, and process controls.
* Lead cross-functional transformation and productivity initiatives, including process redesign, technology-enabled improvement, automation, and new ways of working, in partnership with functional leaders, the PMO, Finance, and other stakeholders.
* Establish measurable outcomes, baselines, KPI definitions, reporting standards, dashboards, and processes for tracking, validating, and sustaining financial benefits, productivity improvements, and business value.
* Build organizational Continuous Improvement capability through training, coaching, structured problem-solving, knowledge sharing, and the development of CI team members and functional leaders.
* Lead change management and cross-functional alignment, manage risks and barriers, strengthen process integration, and communicate priorities, progress, results, and recommendations to Supply Chain leadership and key stakeholders.

**What You’ll Bring**
In addition to the technical and functional requirements of this role, successful candidates demonstrate Domino's Hungry for MORE Ways of Working:
 
 
Be Curious
 
 

* Seeks clarity, asks thoughtful questions, and uncovers root causes to solve problems effectively.
* Actively pursues learning opportunities, applies feedback, and continuously develops new skills.

Connect the Dots
 
 

* Uses information and insights to identify opportunities and drive informed decisions.
* Builds strong partnerships across teams and considers the broader organizational impact of decisions.

Aim High
 
 

* Sets ambitious goals, challenges the status quo, and focuses on work that drives meaningful business results.
* Uses feedback and data to continuously improve performance and outcomes.

Shift Fast
 
 

* Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining focus on results.
* Demonstrates resilience, sound judgment, and the ability to learn from setbacks.

Deliver More
 
 

* Takes ownership, executes with discipline, and consistently produces measurable results.
* Identifies opportunities to create additional value for customers, team members, and the business.

Leadership Expectations
 
 

* Builds and develops high-performing teams aligned to Domino’s Ways of Working.
* Creates accountability, fosters collaboration, and delivers results through others.
* Leads confidently through change while maintaining team engagement and performance.
* Demonstrates enterprise thinking and drives cross-functional alignment to achieve business goals.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline; an advanced degree or MBA is preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, business transformation, operational excellence, or related disciplines, including demonstrated leadership experience in complex, cross-functional organizations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing Continuous Improvement strategies and delivering measurable business results across multiple functions or complex organizations.
* Strong knowledge and practical application of Lean Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, process optimization, standardization, and change management methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional improvement initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive organizational change without direct authority.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience leading Continuous Improvement initiatives in manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or other complex operational environments, including the ability to engage frontline employees, site leaders, and senior executives to diagnose issues, implement solutions, and deliver measurable results.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience identifying, quantifying, and validating productivity improvements, cost savings, and business value.
* Well-developed team building and influencing skills, unquestioned integrity, and the experience and confidence to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
* Experience developing performance management frameworks, leveraging data analytics, and translating insights into actionable business recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to build organizational capability through coaching, talent development, and deployment of Continuous Improvement methodologies.
* Strong strategic thinking, communication, collaboration, and executive presentation skills.
* Experience managing complex improvement portfolios, prioritizing competing business needs, and delivering sustainable outcomes.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent demonstrated Continuous Improvement expertise is preferred.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including Canada, as business needs require. Expected travel is up to 50%

Additional Information
 
 
Benefits:
 
 

* Paid Holidays and Vacation
* Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
* No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
* Childcare tuition discounts
* No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
* Fertility benefits
* Adoption assistance
* 401k matching contributions
* 15% off the purchase price of stock
* Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
