new_roles.title: Sr. Director of Quality
new_roles.description:
The Senior Director of Quality is responsible for leading quality, regulatory compliance, and functions at an assigned facility while providing strategic leadership, guidance, and support to Quality departments across multiple FCAH locations and operating companies. This role ensures compliance with applicable FAA, EASA, customer, and industry requirements while driving consistency in quality standards, processes, audit readiness, corrective actions, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

The Senior Director serves as a hands-on quality leader at their assigned location while partnering with site leadership and other Quality leaders to strengthen quality systems, address regulatory and operational risks, develop quality teams, and promote a culture of accountability, safety, and excellence across the organization.

**Essential Job Functions:**

**Site Quality Leadership**

* Lead and manage the Quality department at the assigned facility, ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company requirements.
* Partner with site leadership, Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other departments to integrate quality into daily operations and decision-making.
* Oversee site quality personnel, including staffing, performance management, training, development, and accountability.
* Ensure the facility maintains required certifications, approvals, manuals, procedures, and quality systems.
* Monitor site quality performance, identify areas of risk, and develop action plans to address deficiencies and improve operational performance.

**Multi-Site Quality Leadership & Support**

* Provide leadership, guidance, and support to Quality departments and leaders across other First Class Air operating companies and locations.
* Partner with site Quality leaders to identify challenges, strengthen quality processes, and improve regulatory compliance and operational effectiveness.
* Promote consistency in quality standards, processes, procedures, and best practices across locations where appropriate.
* Assist other locations with quality initiatives, regulatory concerns, audit preparation, corrective actions, customer issues, and process improvement efforts.
* Conduct site visits to evaluate quality systems, identify opportunities for improvement, and provide support to local Quality teams.
* Share lessons learned, recurring quality issues, and best practices across locations to prevent repeat findings and improve overall organizational performance.
* Help develop and implement company-wide quality initiatives while allowing for site-specific requirements, certifications, and regulatory differences.
* Escalate significant regulatory, operational, customer, or quality risks to executive leadership.

**Regulatory Compliance & Oversight**

* Ensure compliance with applicable FAA, EASA, UK CAA, , customer, and other regulatory requirements, as applicable to company operations.
* Maintain strong working knowledge of FAA regulations, including Part 145, Part 43, and Part 21, as applicable.
* Serve as a point of contact for regulatory authorities, customer representatives, and external auditors, as appropriate.
* Monitor regulatory changes and ensure applicable requirements are communicated and implemented across affected locations.
* Ensure maintenance, repair, overhaul, inspection, manufacturing, and other applicable activities are performed in accordance with approved technical data, regulatory requirements, and established procedures.
* Maintain organizational readiness for regulatory, customer, and third-party audits.

**Quality Management Systems**

* Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve Quality Management Systems (QMS) at the assigned location and across other locations as needed.
* Establish and promote consistent quality standards, policies, procedures, and best practices across the organization.
* Oversee the development, revision, and implementation of quality manuals, procedures, inspection programs, and supporting documentation.
* Ensure appropriate document control, records management, inspection processes, calibration programs, personnel qualifications, training, and other critical quality system controls are maintained.
* Partner with site and enterprise leadership to improve quality processes, reduce risk, and enhance operational performance.

**Audits, Corrective Actions & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead and oversee internal, external, regulatory, customer, and third-party audits at the assigned facility.
* Support and provide guidance to other locations in preparation for and execution of audits.
* Develop and support risk-based audit schedules and audit strategies.
* Ensure audit findings and quality issues are appropriately investigated, contained, corrected, and documented.
* Oversee corrective and preventive action (CAPA) processes and ensure root cause analysis is appropriately performed.
* Verify corrective actions are effective and prevent recurring issues.
* Identify recurring findings, systemic quality issues, and trends across locations and implement improvements where appropriate.

**Airworthiness & Technical Quality**

* Provide oversight of airworthiness and return-to-service processes across applicable repair station operations.
* Ensure appropriate controls are maintained for FAA Form 8130-3, EASA Form 1, inspection, certification, and related airworthiness documentation, as applicable.
* Ensure receiving, in-process, and final inspections are performed in accordance with applicable procedures and requirements.
* Oversee the management and control of capability lists, personnel authorizations, technician and inspector qualifications, stamps, and related records.
* Ensure calibration programs and control of tools, equipment, and test instruments meet applicable requirements.
* Assist other locations with technical quality concerns, inspection processes, airworthiness issues, and regulatory interpretations as needed.

**Customer & Supplier Quality**

* Provide leadership and support in resolving significant customer quality concerns, escalations, and recurring issues.
* Partner with Sales, Operations, Maintenance, and other departments to ensure customer quality expectations are understood and met.
* Monitor supplier-related quality trends and recurring issues.
* Support supplier corrective actions, quality investigations, and improvement initiatives as needed.
* Serve as a quality escalation resource for customer and supplier issues across locations.

**Quality Performance, Reporting & Risk Management**

* Establish and monitor quality performance metrics, KPIs, trends, and reporting processes for the assigned facility.
* Support the development and implementation of company-wide quality dashboards and performance metrics.
* Evaluate quality data to identify trends, recurring issues, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
* Communicate significant quality concerns, regulatory risks, audit findings, and improvement initiatives to site leadership and executive leadership.
* Partner with leadership to prioritize quality initiatives and allocate resources appropriately.
* Provide visibility into quality performance across locations and recommend actions to improve overall company performance.

**Requirements:**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in aviation, aerospace, MRO, manufacturing, or another highly regulated environment.
* Minimum of 7 years of progressive leadership experience in Quality, Regulatory Compliance,, Inspection, or related functions preferred.
* Significant experience leading Quality functions within aviation maintenance, repair, overhaul, manufacturing, or FAA-certified repair station environments.
* Experience supporting multiple departments, facilities, locations, or business units.
* Experience working directly with FAA, EASA, UK CAA, customer representatives, or other regulatory authorities preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading regulatory, customer, internal, and external audits.
* Experience developing, implementing, and maintaining Quality Management Systems.
* Strong working knowledge of FAA regulations, particularly Part 145, Part 43, and Part 21, as applicable.
* Knowledge of EASA, UK CAA,, and other applicable regulatory requirements preferred.
* Strong understanding of Quality Management Systems (QMS), corrective and preventive action (CAPA), root cause analysis, risk management, audit processes, and continuous improvement.
* Ability to interpret technical data, regulatory requirements, manuals, procedures, engineering documentation, and quality standards.
* This role will require 20%-30% travel to other facilities

new_roles.title: Director of Quality Assurance & CI
new_roles.description:
**Lead the Transformation. Build a Culture of Excellence. Deliver Results That Last.**

The Director of Quality Assurance & Continuous Improvement provides strategic leadership for the company's quality and continuous improvement functions, ensuring products, processes, and services consistently meet the highest standards of quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction. This role is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving the Quality Management System (QMS) while driving a culture of operational excellence across the organization. Leading enterprise-wide Lean initiatives, Kaizen events, root cause analysis, and structured continuous improvement programs, this position delivers measurable improvements in quality, productivity, cost, and operational performance. Working closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, the Director establishes quality strategies, drives compliance with customer and regulatory requirements, and champions sustainable improvements that support the company's strategic growth objectives.

**What Success looks Like**

* Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the company's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry standards, including ISO certifications.
* Establish enterprise-wide quality strategies, policies, and governance while serving as the executive leader for quality-related decisions impacting customers, operations, and suppliers.
* Drive a culture of operational excellence by leading Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and structured continuous improvement initiatives across all business functions.
* Develop and execute strategic cost reduction initiatives that improve productivity, eliminate waste, reduce the Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), and enhance overall operational performance.
* Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Sales, and executive leadership to identify, prioritize, and deliver sustainable business improvements.
* Champion the voice of the customer by leveraging customer feedback, warranty data, and field performance to improve product quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction.
* Lead enterprise-wide root cause analysis and corrective action processes to resolve quality issues, prevent recurrence, and strengthen operational performance.
* Oversee internal and external audit programs, ensuring compliance with quality, safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements while proactively managing organizational risk.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing Quality and Continuous Improvement organization while coaching leaders throughout the business to embed a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Establish, monitor, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) that measure quality, delivery, cost savings, productivity, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement performance.
* Translate strategic business objectives into measurable quality and operational improvement initiatives that deliver sustainable financial and operational results.
* Build trusted relationships across the organization and with external stakeholders, influencing decision-making and driving alignment to achieve the company's strategic objectives.

**Qualifications That Shine**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master's degree or other advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive quality leadership experience, including 10+ years leading people and 5+ years leading corporate or multi-site quality organizations.
* Proven success developing and leading Quality Management Systems (QMS) within a manufacturing environment, including ISO implementation, certification, and ongoing compliance.
* Professional certifications such as ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, and Lean certification are strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated success leading Lean transformation, Kaizen events, and enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives that deliver measurable business results.
* Strong knowledge of quality systems, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), statistical process control (SPC), and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to influence executive leadership and build collaborative partnerships across operations, engineering, supply chain, finance, and commercial teams.
* Exceptional communication, presentation, and organizational skills with the ability to translate strategy into execution and drive organizational change.
* Strategic, data-driven leader with a track record of improving quality, operational performance, customer satisfaction, and financial results through operational excellence initiatives.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here**

* **You’ll Be Empowered** **–** You’ll have autonomy in your role, supported by a team that trusts your judgment
* **You’ll Grow With Us** **–** We invest in your training, development, and long-term career path
* **You’ll Be Rewarded** **–** Competitive pay, performance incentives, 401(k) with profit sharing, and great benefits
* **You’ll Make a Real Impact** **–** Your work supports businesses across North America and shapes the future of finishing technology
* **You’ll Join a Great Team** **–** We’re growing fast, we value collaboration, and are committed to your success

**Transparent Rewards** 
 
At GFS, we recognize the dedication behind every role and ensure that our compensation reflects both your impact and our shared success.

**Pay Range:** $124,518 – $156,746 per year, based on your experience, skills, and qualifications.

**Bonus Eligibility:** This position is eligible for an annual individual incentive based on company performance. Maximum bonus amounts may vary depending on role.

**Benefits:** Eligible for standard company benefits, including health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, paid time off, and other employee programs. More detailed information is available at 2026 GFS Benefits.

Actual compensation will be determined by factors including experience, education, certifications, skill level, and market conditions. For remote or hybrid positions, the listed pay range applies to applicants in the specified location.

**About GFS**

Global Finishing Solutions is the leading manufacturer of paint booths and finishing systems serving automotive, aerospace, industrial manufacturing, marine, military, rail, trucking, and wood finishing markets. We specialize in building custom solutions that meet each customer’s unique needs—and we do it with a team that thrives on collaboration and innovation because we're different.

What makes us different is our unwavering commitment to our core values of family, respect, partnership, improvement, and integrity. We are a family-oriented organization that still values the little things, creating a workplace where you can thrive, fairness guides every decision, and collaboration drives shared success. Small town in spirit but big-hearted in impact, here you’re not just joining a company—you’re joining a team that grows together, celebrates together, and builds lasting value together. That’s the difference. Join us.

Apply now at www.gfscareers.us

About GFS 
Watch Us in Action 
Connect on LinkedIn

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

***GFS is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants***. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or any other status protected by law. Employment offers are subject to successful completion of pre-employment drug screening and physicals, consistent with applicable laws.

*Note to recruiters: GFS only works with agencies that have signed a contract with our HR team. Resumes sent directly to hiring managers without a prior agreement are considered unsolicited and the property of GFS. Placement fees will not be paid without a formal contract.*

new_roles.title: Director, Operations & Quality Compliance
new_roles.description:
**Summary**

We are seeking a Director, Global Safety Operations & Quality Management to provide strategic, operational, and technical leadership across Immunic's PV operations, quality management, compliance, and inspection readiness activities for our development and post-marketing portfolio, reporting to the VP of Pharmacovigilance & Patient Safety as a key member of the Global PV leadership team. You will oversee global safety reporting, ICSR processing, aggregate reporting, safety surveillance, quality management systems, compliance, and inspection readiness, ensuring PV activities are governed, risk-based, and scalable, while providing executive-level oversight of CROs, vendors, and external service providers to ensure governance, performance management, and continuous improvement of outsourced PV activities.This is a highly collaborative and strategic role, where you must operate effectively in an evolving biotech to translate regulatory and business requirements into practical operating models, and build high-performing teams and sustainable PV capabilities.

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and implement pharmacovigilance processes, policies, SOPs, and safety database/PV systems.
* Lead cross-functional governance, benefit-risk assessment, signal detection, and risk management efforts.
* Chair the executive safety review committee, oversee safety data exchange with partners, and contribute to industry-wide safety initiatives.
* Partner with clinical development to integrate safety into protocols, risk management plans, and safety charters.
* Provide PV oversight for regulatory filings (IND/BLA/MAA) - including Clinical Overviews, ISS, and RMPs - and review IBs, DSURs, and key CSR sections; participate in regulatory meetings as needed.
* Lead medical review of ICSRs and oversee PV team operations, quality, and compliance with global safety regulations.
* Monitor and assess CRO performance on pharmacovigilance activities.
* Recruit, hire, train, mentor, and coach PV staff, and oversee project deliverables and performance evaluations.

**Qualifications & Education**

* Healthcare professional (RN, PharmD, MD) with clinical and industry experience and a proven track record leading pharmacovigilance teams.
* Minimum of 15 years' experience in drug safety and pharmacovigilance roles in the biotech or pharmaceutical industry.
* Proven leadership expertise, including a track record of building and leading high-performing teams.
* In-depth knowledge of global pharmacovigilance regulations and compliance requirements (EMA/FDA/ICH).
* Strong leadership and strategic decision-making abilities to drive safety initiatives and ensure regulatory compliance.

Immunic Therapeutics is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status.

**Please note, Immunic does not accept unsolicited resumes from external agencies or recruiters. Submission of a resume without a prior written agreement does not create any express or implied contract between Immunic and the agency. Immunic will not pay any fees related to unsolicited resumes.**

Compensation Range: $220K - $260K

new_roles.title: Health, Safety, Environmental & Quality (HSEQ) Director
new_roles.description:
**Join Ferrovial: Where Innovation Meets Opportunity**
======================================================

Are you ready to elevate your career with a global leader in infrastructure solving complex problems and generating a positive outcome on people’s lives? At **Ferrovial** , we are not just a company; we are a community of innovators and trailblazers. Ferrovial is also leading the development of the New Terminal One at JFK International Airport. Ferrovial shares trade under the ticker symbol FER on two stock markets: Nasdaq in the U.S. (Nasdaq100 Index) and the Spanish Stock Exchanges (IBEX 35). Ferrovial is included in globally recognized sustainability indices such as the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Index. We operate in more than 15 countries and have a workforce of over 22,000 professionals worldwide. Ferrovial’s activity is carried out through our business units, including Highways, Airports, Construction, and Energy.

 

Ferrovial’s activity is carried out through our business units, including Highways, Airports, Construction, and Energy.

 

**Why Ferrovial?**

* **Global presence, local impact** : Be part of a company that is shaping the future of infrastructure worldwide, with challenging roles and projects that make a real difference.
* **Collaborative excellence** : Work alongside talented professionals in a collaborative environment where your ideas and contributions are valued.
* **Inclusive Culture:** Thrive in an innovative and respectful workplace that values every voice, celebrates what makes us unique and turns differences into innovation.
* **Career growth** : Benefit from global and cross-business unit mobility, with development processes designed to ensure your professional growth.
* **Compelling benefits and employee wellbeing** : Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that rewards your hard work and dedication and take advantage of initiatives designed to support your physical and psychological health.
* **Productivity tools** : Utilize cutting-edge tools like Microsoft Copilot to enhance your productivity and efficiency.

 

**Job Description:**
====================

**About the role:**

The HSEQ Director develops and implements health, safety, environmental, and quality programs for I-24 Mobility Partners and ensures compliance with OSHA, U.S. DOT, EPA, and Tennessee requirements. The Director owns the Quality Management System and Quality Management Plan, verifies program effectiveness through audits, inspections, and investigations, and has authority to stop work when there is an imminent hazard to people, property, or the environment.

 

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Review design-builder and sub-consultant quality and safety plans for alignment with the concessionaire's plans, and work with the Chief Infrastructure Officer on quality oversight of design and construction.

* Liaise with TDOT, the design-builder, the independent engineer, and external auditors on quality, safety, and environmental matters.

* Develop, implement, and continuously improve HSEQ programs, and communicate regulatory requirements and action plans to the team.

* Oversee the quality management personnel, and document control, and report HSEQ performance to stakeholders.
* Support case management of occupational injuries and illnesses, including light-duty programs, return to work, and workers' compensation information.

* Implement and own the Quality Management System and Quality Management Plan, and fulfill the Quality Manager duties assigned in the concession agreement.

* Stop work when there is an imminent hazard to the health and well-being of employees, property, or the environment.

* Lead periodic Management Reviews of the quality and environmental management systems, and promote compliance with ISO standards.

Evaluate and implement best-in-class AI and digital tools for safety analytics, incident trend detection, inspection and audit management, and document control. 

 

**Qualifications:**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to fulfill those duties. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

***Education & Experience:***

* Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience

* 12 to 15+ years of experience in HSEQ compliance, ideally in construction or transportation infrastructure

* Knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations, including OSHA, EPA, U.S. DOT, DOL, and Tennessee requirements

* Internal and external audit experience (ISO 9001, 14001, and/or 45001)

* Knowledge of the Incident Command System (ICS)

* Ability to complete OSHA 510 and OSHA 500 (OSHA Authorized Outreach Trainer) within 1 year

* Board of Certified Safety Professionals certification, or ability to obtain within 1 year

* Experience implementing or maintaining an ISO or similar certification system preferred

Working knowledge of 40 CFR environmental regulations preferred 

 

***Professional Qualities:***

* Sound judgment and courage: makes timely decisions, including stopping work when required, and stands behind them

* Audit and compliance rigor: verifies that corrective actions work and that standards are met in practice

* Influence at every level: builds relationships quickly and communicates effectively with all levels of the organization, including a culturally diverse workforce

* Clear communication: writes, presents, and speaks with precision on technical safety, environmental, and quality topics

* Analytical problem solving: uses data and trend analysis to find root causes and prevent recurrence

* Digital and AI fluency: applies AI-enabled safety, inspection, and quality tools to detect risk earlier and improve oversight

Ownership and initiative: manages tasks and tight deadlines independently in a fast-paced environment 

 

***Computer Skills:***

Must be able to demonstrate computer proficiency, especially with Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint and other PC based programs 

 

**Work Environment & Physical Demands:**

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* The noise level in the office work environment is usually quiet; noise levels in the field may be loud, requiring hearing protection

* Some travel required, which may include air travel

* The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds

* Specific vision abilities required by this job include the ability to adjust focus, as necessary to use a computer

* While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear

* The employee is frequently required to stand, walk and sit

**Seize the challenge. Move the world together!** Innovative, creative, respectful, and diverse are some of the ways we describe ourselves. We are motivated by challenges, and we collaborate across our business units to move the world together. Your journey to a fulfilling career starts here!

Ferrovial is an equal opportunity employer. We treat all jobs applications equally, regardless of gender, color, race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, covered veteran status or protected genetic information (each, a “Protected Class”), or any other protected class in accordance with applicable laws.

new_roles.title: Director of Quality and Survey
new_roles.description:
At Vetter Senior Living, our mission is simple: **Dignity in Life**. We are a premier provider of long-term care, assisted living, independent living, therapy, and home health and hospice services, and our team of skilled and caring people is committed to making quality service a way of life. Our work is guided by our values of Serving, Integrity, Teamwork, and Excellence.

**About the Role**

We are seeking a Director of Quality and Survey to provide quality and survey leadership and support to our communities. Through strong personal relationships, you will help our communities and service lines ensure that quality and regulatory requirements are not only met but exceeded. This role travels between communities and serves as a trusted clinical and regulatory resource for facility leadership.

### **Benefits**

* Student Loan Repayment Assistance
* Earned Wage Access
* Medical Insurance Options
* Vision Coverage
* Free Individual Dental Insurance
* 401(k) with Employer Match
* Flexible Spending Accounts
* Employee Assistance Program
* Leadership Development Opportunities
* Career Growth and Advancement
* Supportive Senior Leadership Team
* Great Place to Work® Certified Organization

**What You Will Do**

* Monitor compliance with federal and state regulations and maintain ongoing survey readiness in skilled nursing and assisted living.
* Identify potential deficiencies early and help facility leadership develop corrective actions.
* Conduct focused and routine audits of high-risk areas such as falls, wounds, infections, medication management, hospital transfers, documentation, and changes in condition.
* Manage the iQIES and HARP systems for the organization.
* Support facility Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) activities by identifying trends, establishing improvement plans, monitoring results, and evaluating whether interventions are working.
* Provide targeted education and coaching to Directors of Nursing, nurse leaders, and clinical teams when audits or quality data reveal knowledge or process gaps.
* Drive corrective actions such as staff education, coaching, focused chart reviews, and process changes.
* Serve as a clinical and regulatory resource to facility leadership on complex compliance, resident-care, documentation, or risk concerns.
* Partner with leadership while maintaining facility accountability for day-to-day operations.
* Promote continuous improvement in quality and survey processes and outcomes, and support all Vetter Senior Living service lines and growth opportunities.

**What You Bring**

* Licensed nurse (RN preferred).
Minimum of 3* -5 years of experience in post-acute care.
* Experience managing quality outcomes, with a strong understanding of regulations and survey preparation and management.
* Excellent communication and education skills.
* Strong organizational and relationship-building skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel between communities.
* High personal integrity, a caring attitude, and a genuine desire to work with and support others.

**Why Join Us**

You will be part of a highly respected team of skilled and caring people who are committed to making quality service a way of life. Your daily efforts will help our communities deliver exceptional care, and you will find fulfillment in building relationships, coordinating care, and helping enhance the dignity in people's lives.

**Ready to make a difference? Apply today to join the Vetter Senior Living team.**

new_roles.title: Director, Quality
new_roles.description:
**Position Summary**
--------------------

The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.

Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.

**What You’ll do as a Director Quality**
----------------------------------------

* The Director, Quality will have responsibility for the following: Leads manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality staff in the execution and continuous improvement of the STERIS Quality System. Operates with a focus on the following objectives:
 + Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
 + Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
 + Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
 + Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
 + Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
 + Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
 + Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
 + Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.
* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
* Works closely with the regulatory function to ensure compliance to appropriate ISO and FDA standards; plans for and assists in the management of external audits.
* Leads manufacturing and service site quality teams to ensure alignment to operations, support of Lean efforts and drive quality improvement performance for products, services, and processes across the sites.
* This individual has autonomy to perform the duties of Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) on behalf of STERIS legal manufacturing entities under the EU MDR. This individual shall suffer no disadvantage within the organization in relation to proper fulfilment of his or her duties in lieu of article 15 of the EU MDR.

**The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed**
------------------------------------------------

**Required:**

* Bachelor’s Degree (Engineering or related technical field)
* Minimum 10 years of experience with increased responsibility leading quality system and product quality improvement efforts. Exceptional leadership manifested through organizing and motivating teams toward their respective goals by employing hands-on management.
* Must fulfil the experience requirements listed in Article 15 of the EUMDR (PRRC).
* A solid quality foundation indicated by a demonstrated understanding of Lean/Six Sigma, quality system, and product/process improvement methodologies.
* Solid business acumen and proven ability to build and lead process and product improvement strategies and results.
* Strong expertise in analytical methods, quality systems, and continuous improvement methods.
* Excellent interpersonal, as well as verbal and written communication skills in order to develop and maintain rapport and effective internal and external relationships to support business success.
* The ability to work hard and deliver results under pressure, as well as the willingness to address and shift priorities in rapidly changing markets.

**Preferred:**

* Advanced degree.
* Experience with statistical analysis software and Visio.
* Experience in medical device industry.

**Other:**

* Excellent problem-solving skills.
* Focus on identification of potential issues and continuous improvement.
* Experience working on cross-functional teams and on own initiative.
* Demonstrated excellent organizational, oral, and written communications skills.
* Must have PC experience, as well as working familiarity of desktop applications including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

**What STERIS Offers**
----------------------

We value our employees and are committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, well-being, and financial future.

Here is a brief overview of what we offer:

 

* Market competitive pay
* Extensive paid time off and (9) added holidays
* Excellent healthcare, dental, and vision benefits
* Long/short term disability coverage
* 401(K) with company match
* Maternity and parental leave
* Additional add on benefits/discounts for programs such as pet insurance
* Tuition reimbursement and continued educational programs
* Excellent opportunities for advancement in a stable long-term career

#LI-HT

Pay range for this opportunity is $144,500.00 - $187,000.00. This position is eligible for bonus participation.

Minimum pay rates offered will comply with county/city minimums, if higher than range listed. Pay rates are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to local labor market costs, years of relevant experience, education, professional certifications, foreign language fluency, etc.

STERIS offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits portfolio.

Open until position is filled.

STERIS is a leading global provider of products and services that support patient care with an emphasis on infection prevention. WE HELP OUR CUSTOMERS CREATE A HEALTHIER AND SAFER WORLD by providing innovative healthcare and life sciences products and services around the globe. For more information, visit www.steris.com.

If you need assistance completing the application process, please call 1 (440) 392.7047. This contact information is for accommodation inquiries only and cannot be used to check application status.

new_roles.title: Director, Quality GxP Vendor Management & Audit Programs
new_roles.description:
Description:

**The Company:**

This publicly held clinical-stage biotechnology company is focused on developing treatments for patients suffering from complex rare diseases using its novel cell penetrating peptide technology platform. Their lead product candidate, nomlabofusp, is a subcutaneously administered, recombinant fusion protein intended to deliver human frataxin (FXN), an essential protein to the mitochondria of patients with Friedreich’s ataxia. Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, progressive, and fatal disease in which patients are unable to produce sufficient FXN due to a genetic abnormality.

The company has 80 employees and has assembled an experienced management team, each of whom has over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience. The management team, employees, and consultants have significant expertise in discovery, nonclinical and clinical development, regulatory affairs, commercialization, and the development of manufacturing processes utilizing good manufacturing practices (GMPs).

The company’s strategy is to become a leader in the treatment of rare diseases by leveraging their technology platform and applying their team’s know-how and expertise to the development of CTI-1601 and other future pipeline programs. They are best characterized by entrepreneurial and scientific leadership and a participatory workforce committed to success.

**Position Summary:**

The Director, GxP Vendor Management is responsible for leading Larimar’s GxP vendor management and audit programs and collaborating with key functional area stakeholders to ensure vendors are selected, qualified, managed and overseen in compliance with Larimar and regulatory requirements. This role owns the full vendor lifecycle and will shape the program’s strategy as Larimar seeks BLA approval, progresses with Phase 3 trial and plans for commercialization.

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead and implement the strategic direction of the vendor management and audit programs at Larimar.
* Own the risk-based vendor qualification framework, including risk tiering and minimum oversight expectations for each tier, and manage day-to-day qualification activities through vendor audit and assessment, qualification, approval and filing of vendor-related qualification documentation.
* Maintain an approved vendor list and a master tracker of all GxP vendors (current, historic, and planned) as the single source of truth for vendor qualification/requalification, audit, and Quality Agreements.
* Partner with functional areas to develop and oversee execution of the risk-based annual external audit plan, including auditor assignments, audit tracking, follow up of audit responses and CAPAs, and filing of audit documentation.
* Manage the internal audit program including development and execution of internal audit plan to adequately assess Larimar’s internal processes.
* Manage the Quality Agreement program, including development and maintenance of Quality Agreements, and partner with Legal and functional areas to ensure Quality Agreements are in place and current with applicable vendors.
* Partner with functional areas to develop, review and maintain risk-based vendor oversight plans, including expectations for KPIs; governance meetings; issue escalation; oversight activities, frequency, responsibility, and documentation requirements; and verification that vendors and their subcontractors use qualified personnel.
* Conduct training on vendor management and audit programs to ensure functional areas understand and appropriately execute their responsibilities.
* Partner with functional areas to identify vendor deviations to assess issues potentially impacting the vendor qualification status or required oversight.
* Develop Vendor Management metrics, analyze vendor performance and compliance trends, and lead a periodic cross-functional vendor review that feeds into Quality Management Review.
* Ensure inspection readiness in the vendor management function and assist functional areas with readiness related to selection, qualification, management and oversight of their vendors.
* Evaluate and implement electronic vendor management systems, as applicable.

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* BS/BA in a life science or related field, or equivalent industry experience.
* 10+ years’ experience in the Pharmaceutical/Biotechnology industry, including at least 5 years leading vendor management/audit programs in a GxP environment.
* Expert knowledge of FDA, EMA, MHRA and ICH GxP regulations and guidelines, including ICH E6(R3) expectations for sponsor oversight of service providers.
* Strong GxP foundation associated with vendor oversight.
* Demonstrated experience planning and managing GxP vendor and internal audits, including follow up of audit responses and CAPAs.
* Experience developing and negotiating Quality Agreements with CROs, laboratories and other GxP service providers.
* Proficient with Veeva Systems, including Veeva Vault QualityDocs, desirable.
* Experience applying risk-based approaches to vendor tiering and oversight.
* Strong communication skills with all levels of the organization and external vendors, and the ability to influence functional areas without direct authority.
* Excellent organizational skills, analytical and problem-solving abilities, and strong verbal and writing skills.

**Benefits:**

Larimar Therapeutics offers all employees incentive stock options, a comprehensive benefits plan including 401K, and a flexible PTO policy.

***Equal Opportunity Employment***

*We are committed to equal-employment principles, and we recognize the value of committed employees who feel they are being treated in an equitable and professional manner. We strive to find ways to attract, develop and retain the talent needed to meet business objectives, and to recruit and employ highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities in which we live.*

*Employment policies and decisions on employment and promotion are based on merit, qualifications, performance, and business needs. The decisions and criteria governing the employment relationship with all employees are made in a non-discriminatory manner—without regard to age, race, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical condition related to pregnancy or childbirth), gender identity or expression, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, marital status, veteran status, military status, sexual orientation, or any other factor determined to be an unlawful basis for such decisions by federal, state, or local statutes.*

new_roles.description:
**Employment Type:** 
Full time
 
 
**Shift:** 
Day Shift
 
 
**Description:** 
The Eddy’s continuing care network, including a wide range of services—from nursing homes, assisted living, independent living, memory care, home health, hospice, PACE, infusion pharmacy to durable medical equipment—has an exciting and rewarding opportunity for a RN Director of Quality& Safety to work with teams across our network
 
 
Key responsibilities related to quality improvement include but are not limited to:
 
 

* Supporting the development of QAPI plans, goals and metrics
* Supporting and preparing reports for three Divisional QAPI Committees (Community-Based Services, Nursing Homes, and Senior Living)
* Gathering and presenting quality and safety data to the Board Quality& Safety Committee across all service lines
* Representing The Eddy Continuing Care services in a wide range of quality-related meetings
* Overall education and support of leaders across the network in continuously improving quality and outcomes

**Key responsibilities related to Safety include:** 

* Educating and support colleagues
* Facilitating meetings and the work of Safety Champions at each location
* Representing The Eddy Continuing Care Network in a wide range of Safety& Risk Management related meetings
* Preparing a wide range of reports summarizing safety/risk management related data across all service lines and development of presentations

**Education:** 

* BSN Required; MSN preferred

**Experience:** 

* Quality improvement, safety/risk management.
* Experience working in at least one continuing care service line a plus but not required (nursing homes, assisted living, independent living, memory care, home health, hospice, PACE).
* Requires expertise in using a wide range of software programs (EPIC and PCC Electronic Medical Records, MIDAS, etc.)
* Preparing concise SBARs summarizing incidents
* PowerPoint, Excel and other programs in the presentation of quality and safety data/trends, etc.

**Pay Range:** 
$116,480-$153,795.20
 
Pay is based on experience, skills, and education. Exempt positions under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) will be paid within the base salary equivalent of the stated hourly rates. The pay range may also vary within the stated range based on location.

By finding common ground and embracing our differences, we grow stronger together and deliver more compassionate, person-centered care. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. new_roles.title: Director, Quality Operations
new_roles.description:
**Revvity**

Revvity is a developer and provider of end-to-end solutions designed to help scientists, researchers, and clinicians solve the world’s greatest health challenges. We pair the enthusiasm of an industry disruptor with the experience of a longtime leader. Our team of 11,000+ colleagues from around the globe are vital to our success and the reason we’re able to push boundaries in pursuit of better human health.

Find your future at Revvity.

Our team is seeking a Director, Quality Operations to lead site quality for the Hopkinton-based operation. This role succeeds the current site quality leadership position and is intentionally scoped at the Director level because it combines broad operational accountability, organizational build-out, and a significant quality-system integration mandate. The Director will lead a blended Quality Operations organization spanning product quality, quality systems, supplier and incoming quality, inspection, and production support. The successful leader must protect ongoing product quality and compliance while progressively simplifying, integrating, and modernizing the operating model.

 
 

**Routine Responsibilities:**
-----------------------------

**Site Quality Leadership and Governance**
------------------------------------------

* Quality Operations leader for Hopkinton, with accountability for product quality, manufacturing quality, inspection, release, and site QMS execution.

* Provide visible, hands-on leadership in production and laboratory environments, enabling rapid risk-based decisions and timely escalation of material, process, product, and compliance issues.

* Own the site quality operating rhythm, including management review, quality metrics, risk review, resource prioritization, and cross-functional governance with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, R&D, Regulatory, Service, and Commercial teams.

* Serve as the principal site Quality representative for FDA, ISO, notified-body, customer, and internal audits, and ensure sustained inspection readiness across the blended operation.

* Balance product continuity, customer commitments, compliance, and transformation priorities using documented risk-based decisions.

 
 

**QMS, SOP, and Digital-System Integration**
--------------------------------------------

* Create and execute a phased roadmap improve and sustain SOPs and QMS structures supporting the site, with clear process ownership, sequencing, change controls, validation needs, and business-continuity safeguards.

* Optimize operating model for document control, production records, training, calibration, internal audits, supplier management, incoming inspection, final acceptance, complaints, and customer field interfaces.

* Lead the integration and modernization of quality tools and records currently distributed across systems and methods.

* Partner with enterprise Quality, Regulatory, IT/Digital, and business process owners to deploy scalable solutions and eliminate duplicate or conflicting workflows, records, and controls.

* Ensure data integrity, validated-state control, traceability, retention, access, and training are maintained throughout system and process transitions.

 
 

**Product and Manufacturing Quality**
-------------------------------------

* Lead quality support for a diverse portfolio that includes instruments, consumables and reagents platforms.

* Oversee incoming inspection, in-process controls, final product acceptance and release, nonconformance and material-review processes, manufacturing investigations, and CAPA effectiveness.

* Ensure appropriate validation and verification of manufacturing processes, equipment, software-enabled tools, inspection methods, and test methods.

* Drive preventive product-quality improvements using defect, yield, scrap, complaint, service, supplier, and Cost of Poor Quality trends.

* Represent Quality in design transfer, manufacturing transfer, new-product introduction, supplier changes, capacity expansion, and sustaining-engineering decisions.

 
 

**Organization Build and People Leadership**
--------------------------------------------

* Lead and develop a multi-disciplinary team of Quality Systems, Product Quality, Supplier/Incoming Quality, Quality Control, inspection, technician, and specialist roles.

* Implement planned organization expansion, including Quality Systems leadership, compliance coordination, QC supervision, and temporary integration support, while clarifying accountability across product and system responsibilities.

* Build succession depth and technical capability through coaching, performance management, role clarity, development plans, and targeted cross-training across legacy product and QMS environments.

* Set clear performance expectations and foster a culture of ownership, constructive challenge, timely decision-making, and practical continuous improvement.

* Plan resource needs and manage the site Quality Operations budget, contractor usage, and external support in line with the operating plan.

 
 

**Customer, Supplier, and Compliance Interface**
------------------------------------------------

* Own the Quality Operations response to significant customer issues, quality agreements, customer audits, field escalations, and product-quality communications in partnership with Commercial Quality and Regulatory.

* Provide governance for supplier quality and incoming-quality activities, including risk-based controls, supplier corrective action, change assessment, and escalation of supply continuity risks.

* Ensure complaints, quality events, CAPAs, deviations, nonconformances, and risk-management activities are documented, investigated, assessed, and closed with appropriate rigor and timeliness.

* Responsible for customer complaint handling and investigations in collaboration with cross functional teams driving problem solving and resolution plans.

Maintain effective QMS training, document control, internal audit, calibration, and records-management programs across the site scope.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* bachelors degree
* 15+ years of quality experience with 7+ years management experience
 

 

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience supporting instruments, reagents and consumable product lines and systems.
* Experience deploying or consolidating eQMS, ERP, PLM, inspection, training, document-control, or calibration systems.
* Lean, Six Sigma, ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, or comparable credentials.
* Experience hosting regulatory and customer audits and managing complex customer-quality interfaces.
* Experience with data analysis, analytics, and management reporting schemes.
 

 

**Physical Requirements & Expectations:**

* The primary working condition associated with this position is working independently in the office environment.
* It is frequently required to work cross-functionally. Travel may be required up to 10%.
* Requires the ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds, sit and/or stand for prolonged periods of time and effectively manage conflict and emotional or stressful situations.
* Potential hazards associated with blood products.

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to the role.

 
 

**Compensation Range:**

The annual base salary range for this full-time position is $159,000 - $185,000. This range reflects the minimum and maximum target for a new hire in this position. The base pay actually offered to the successful candidate will take into account internal equity, work location, and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

Please note that base pay is only one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This range allows for the successful candidate to have an opportunity to progress within the position and develop at our company. This base pay range does not take into account bonuses, equity, or other benefits which may be applicable and are dependent on the level and position offered.

#LI-CH1

 
 
 

**What do we offer?**

We provide competitive and comprehensive benefits to our employees. Below are some highlights of our benefits:

* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance Options
* Life and Disability Insurance
* Paid Time-Off
* Parental Benefits
* Compassionate Care Leave
* 401k with Company Match
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan

Learn more about Revvity’s benefits by visiting our Bswift (opens in new window) page. Log-In instructions are provided towards the bottom of the Bswift page.

*For benefit-eligible roles only. Part-time and temporary roles may not be eligible for all benefits listed. Please reach out to your recruiter for more information.*

**Recruitment Scam Alert**

We've become aware that scammers are impersonating members of our recruitment team by using fake email addresses and fraudulent job opportunities.

Please remember:

We will never ask you to pay for an interview, job offer, equipment, training, or any part of our recruitment process. Always verify that recruitment emails come from our official company email domain (revvity.com). Revvity will never conduct interviews via text message, messaging apps, or social media direct messages. If you're ever unsure whether a recruitment message is genuine, please contact us through our official careers website before responding.
 
 
Your safety is important to us.
 
If you believe you've been targeted by recruitment fraud in the United States, you can report it to the Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) at https://www.ic3.gov/ or the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov .

new_roles.title: Head of Global Quality Strategic Initiatives
new_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Head of Global Quality Strategic Initiatives is responsible for defining, leading and executing enterprise-wide initiatives that strengthen TransMedics’ global quality management system (QMS), enhance regulatory compliance, improve product quality and patient safety, and advance operational excellence across the product lifecycle.

Partnering closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, this leader translates business priorities into measurable quality outcomes. The role drives complex transformation programs, anticipates emerging quality and regulatory risks, and establishes the processes, governance and metrics needed to support growth while maintaining high standards of safety, effectiveness and compliance.

The successful candidate combines deep medical device quality and regulatory expertise with strategic vision, strong business acumen and exceptional program leadership, with the ability to influence at every level of a global organization.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

This position is responsible for, but not limited to, the following:

* Develop and execute a multi-year global quality roadmap aligned with business priorities, regulatory expectations and patient safety. Identify systemic issues and emerging risks, prioritize transformation initiatives, and integrate quality priorities into business planning, product development and growth.
* Lead a portfolio of cross-functional quality programs with clear scope, milestones, resources, accountability and measurable outcomes. Establish executive steering committees, decision rights and escalation paths; resolve barriers, recommend investment priorities and track business impact and sustained results.
* Improve and harmonize the global QMS in line with FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, EU MDR and other applicable requirements. Strengthen process ownership, management review and effectiveness monitoring while accommodating regional requirements and local operating needs.
* Oversee improvement programs spanning document and records management, design and manufacturing controls, risk management, supplier quality, nonconformance, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), change control and post-market processes.
* Partner with Regulatory Affairs and site Quality leaders to assess regulatory changes and lead enterprise remediation programs addressing audit findings, regulatory observations and emerging risks. Support FDA inspections and external audits, resolve root causes, and embed sustainable inspection readiness.
* Define enterprise quality KPIs and key risk indicators covering CAPA effectiveness, complaints, nonconformances, audit findings, suppliers and product quality. Build consistent dashboards and executive reporting that improve visibility into risks, trends and program progress.
* Sponsor electronic QMS, quality data integration, advanced analytics and appropriate AI-enabled initiatives within applicable validation, privacy, security and regulatory controls. Promote data integrity, traceability and evidence-based decisions.
* Partner with functional leaders to strengthen product risk management, complaint handling, adverse event reporting, field action assessment and post-market monitoring from development and design transfer through manufacturing and post-market surveillance. Lead analysis of recurring issues and systemic failure modes to improve detection, containment and prevention.
* Apply Lean, Six Sigma and risk-based problem-solving to reduce rework, scrap, variation and the cost of poor quality while protecting compliance and patient safety. Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain and site leaders to improve process capability and supplier performance, replicate best practices and measure benefits.
* Advise the Chief Regulatory Officer and executive leadership on quality priorities, systemic risks and transformation opportunities; communicate with the Board as appropriate. Influence priorities and resource decisions, mentor quality and program leaders, and lead training and change management that build accountability, transparency and lasting quality ownership.
* Collaborate with IT/Digital, Finance, Human Resources and other internal partners, and engage regulatory authorities, notified and certification bodies, external auditors, strategic suppliers, consultants and industry organizations as needed.
* Success will be measured by on-time transformation milestones; stronger QMS effectiveness and consistency; fewer recurring issues, overdue corrective actions and repeat audit findings; sustained inspection readiness; and measurable improvements in product quality, complaint trends, supplier performance and cost of poor quality.
* Perform other TransMedics tasks and duties as assigned.

**MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES**

Convene and lead cross-functional teams, establish program governance, and develop and mentor quality and program leaders within the approved mandate, budget and governance structure. Direct-report responsibilities are to be confirmed. Formal authority for regulatory decisions, product disposition, quality approvals and regulatory reporting remains with the accountable functions under company procedures.

**PHYSICAL ATTRIBUTES**

This is an on-site role in Andover or Somerville, MA, with approximately 10–20% travel. Additional essential physical requirements, if applicable, are to be confirmed.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, Regulatory Affairs or a related technical discipline.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in medical devices, combination products or another highly regulated healthcare industry, including significant leadership experience in Quality, Regulatory Affairs, quality transformation or enterprise program management.
* Proven success leading complex quality improvement, remediation or organizational change programs across business units, manufacturing sites and geographies, translating strategy into executable plans and measurable, sustainable results.
* Strong knowledge of FDA medical device requirements, including QMSR, and working knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 14971, EU MDR and applicable global medical device frameworks.
* Hands-on experience with CAPA, nonconformances, complaints, design controls, supplier quality, change management, audits, remediation and post-market surveillance; understanding of root cause analysis, process validation, manufacturing controls and QMS effectiveness.
* Familiarity with electronic QMS platforms, quality data analytics and computerized system validation or assurance (CSV/CSA) principles.
* Ability to influence senior executives and stakeholders in a global matrix organization, communicate complex issues clearly, and drive decisions without relying on direct authority.
* Demonstrated strategic thinking, analytical problem-solving, change leadership and talent development, with sound risk-based judgment, integrity and accountability for product quality, patient safety and regulatory compliance.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Business Administration or a related field.
* Professional certifications in quality (ASQ CQE or CMQ/OE), regulatory affairs (RAC), program management (PMP), Lean Six Sigma or change management.
* Experience with MasterControl.

As part of our long-term growth plans, TransMedics is excited to announce our plan to relocate our headquarters (HQ) to Somerville, MA by 2028. We chose this location because we believe it is a place where innovation will thrive. Our new state-of-the-art headquarters is designed to support collaboration, creativity, and discovery. We believe this will be a place where we can continue to do things few thought possible in organ transplantation to help patients. *Specific timing and role impact may vary.*

TransMedics, Inc. is a commercial-stage medical technology company transforming organ transplant therapy for patients worldwide. Our mission is to help save more patients’ lives by increasing access to viable donor organs for those who are awaiting an organ transplant. To accomplish this mission, we partner closely with transplant stakeholders worldwide and help expand their access to healthy donor organs, while delivering the highest quality technology, service, clinical care and outcomes. 
 
Driven by a passion for improving patient care, we make the impossible possible and keep our employees at the center of everything we do. Together, we strive to enhance the quality of life for transplant recipients and their families, fostering hope and healing in the journey toward better health. 
 
**Maximize your potential at TransMedics, Inc.** 
www.TransMedics.com

The expected base salary range for this role is $232,800-$331,350, which represents the company’s current good-faith estimate of compensation for this position. Actual salary will depend on factors such as, but not limited to, candidate experience, qualifications, skills, and the specific work location. This role may also be eligible for bonuses, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental, vision, retirement savings, paid time off, and wellness resources). We comply with all U.S. pay transparency laws and do not request or consider salary history.
