existing_roles.title: Director, QA Ops - Document, Training & Records Management
existing_roles.description:
Looking for a chance to make a meaningful difference in the oncology space? Taiho Oncology is on a mission: to improve the lives of patients with cancer, their families, and caregivers. Our “People first” approach means we also highly value our employees, who work relentlessly to help execute our mission. Taiho’s success is founded on ensuring we always act with accountability, collaboration, and trust. By following these guiding principles, we earn and maintain the confidence of patients, the global healthcare community, collaborators and partners, and each other. Together, we are working on cutting-edge science and growing our portfolio and pipeline across a range of tumor types to address the ongoing and evolving needs of patients. Advanced technology, a world-class clinical development organization, and state-of-the-art facilities: these and other resources empower us to innovate and touch the lives of more and more patients. It’s our work, our passion, and our legacy. We invite you to join us.
  
  
**Hybrid:** 3-days per week on-site
  
Employee Value Proposition
  
​​​​​​At Taiho Oncology, the compassion we practice for our patients extends to our team, empowering and motivating them to do their best work for those who need it most. This is an exciting opportunity to lead critical Quality systems in a dynamic, collaborative, and global cross-functional environment.
  
  
**Position Summary:**  
​​​​​​​​​The Director, QA Ops – Document, Training & Records Management is responsible for the strategy, governance, and execution of Taiho Oncology’s controlled document management, GxP training management, archival, and records-retention programs. This position leads the team responsible for day-to-day activities in MasterControl and establishes scalable processes, system capabilities, and governance that support current operations and Taiho’s future business plans. The Director partners with Quality, functional leaders, Information Technology, system owners, affiliates, and global stakeholders to maintain compliant, efficient, and inspection-ready programs.
  
  
**Performance Objectives:**  
**​​​​Strategy, Governance and Leadership:**  

* Develop and execute the long-term strategy and operating model for controlled document management, GxP training management, archival, and records retention.
* Translate Taiho’s future plans into scalable processes, systems, governance, resources, and program roadmaps.
* Establish policies, standards, performance measures, risk controls, and continuous-improvement priorities and provide recommendations to senior management.
* Lead harmonization and standardization of document and training practices across TOI and applicable affiliates and global stakeholders.
* Manage, coach, and develop the team responsible for document, training, archival, and records-management activities; maintain clear roles, capacity, cross-training, succession planning, and business continuity.

**MasterControl and Quality System Oversight:**  

* Provide business ownership, strategic direction, and governance for MasterControl document and training capabilities.
* Oversee administration of document workflows, courses, curricula, assignments, job codes, user accounts, metadata, effective dates, access, archival status, and related records.
* Partner with Information Technology and validation stakeholders on enhancements, upgrades, integrations, access controls, user acceptance testing, Computer System Assurance documentation, and maintenance of the validated state.
* Evaluate and implement capabilities needed to align MasterControl with business growth, affiliate integration, data integrity, inspection readiness, and future quality-system plans.
* Ensure procedures, user guidance, training materials, reports, and support mechanisms remain current and effective.

**Controlled Document Management:**  

* Oversee the lifecycle management of controlled policies, standard operating procedures, work instructions, forms, guidance documents, and other GxP documents from creation through retirement and archival.
* Establish standards for templates, numbering, naming, metadata, review and approval, effective dates, revision history, periodic review, document relationships, distribution, and supersession.
* Ensure controlled documents receive appropriate Quality and administrative review and that document owners resolve quality, workflow, implementation, and timeliness issues.
* Lead periodic assessment and cleanup of the controlled-document environment, including obsolete, duplicate, or floating documents and attachments.
* Provide document-management leadership and evidence support during audits, inspections, due diligence, and compliance reviews.

**GxP Training Management:**  

* Establish the strategy and governance framework for GxP training across TOI and applicable affiliates.
* Ensure training requirements, curricula, courses, job codes, assignments, and records are aligned with job responsibilities, controlled documents, organizational changes, and compliance obligations.
* Oversee onboarding, role changes, transfers, leaves of absence, and separation processes as they affect training requirements and records.
* Ensure required training is assigned, completed, tracked, documented, reported, and retained; monitor compliance and escalate material risks.
* Oversee new-hire Quality training, document creator/revisor training, instructor-led training, read-and-understand activities, assessments, and other approved training methods.
* Lead improvements that strengthen training effectiveness, learner experience, role alignment, reporting, and inspection readiness.

**Archival and Records Retention:**  

* Develop and oversee the strategy for identification, transfer, storage, protection, retrieval, retention, disposition, and migration of applicable quality records.

In 1896, the enterprising father and son team of A.J. and George A. Briggs partnered with S.A. Buffington, a Chicago lawyer, to establish Chicago Telephone Supply Company (later to become CTS).

Today, CTS is a leading designer and manufacturer of sensors, actuators, and electronic components for suppliers and original equipment manufacturers. We have over 20 locations in 12 countries and more than 3,500 employees. **DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS**

*Ritchey Livestock ID* | Fort Collins, Colorado | Full-Time, Onsite

Run the Operation. Build the Team. Shape What's Next.

**This Role Is For Builders.**

**We're looking for someone who can run a great operation today—and help build the company we'll become tomorrow.**

At Ritchey Livestock ID, we believe farmers and ranchers are the unsung heroes of our world. They work long hours, in every kind of weather, doing the essential work of feeding the rest of us. They don't ask for much in return. The least we can do is get our little part right.

For more than 60 years, we've manufactured livestock identification tags that ranchers can count on. Our products may be small, but the responsibility we feel to our customers is anything but.

We're a profitable, growing American manufacturer with a loyal nationwide customer base. We've recently completed the largest facility investment in our company's history, opening a new manufacturing operation in Fort Collins, Colorado. Now we're building the people, systems, and culture to carry Ritchey into its next chapter.

**We're looking for a hands-on Director of Operations who can lead that effort—and potentially grow into a broader executive leadership role as the company evolves.**

This is not a position for someone who wants to lead from behind a desk. You'll spend meaningful time on the production floor, working alongside your managers, solving real problems, and helping people succeed.

You'll also be expected to think beyond today's production schedule: developing leaders, building systems, improving performance, and preparing Ritchey for its next stage of growth.

**The Opportunity**

You'll lead approximately 45 people across manufacturing, engraving, shipping, and related operations, working directly with our CEO.

Your mission is twofold: **Run an exceptional operation today. Build the people, processes, and accountability that make excellence repeatable tomorrow.**

You'll own performance across safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, cost, and team development.

You'll be responsible for developing department managers, improving operational systems, driving continuous improvement, and building a culture where people take pride in their work and ownership of their results.

**Your First Year: Real Challenges, Real Opportunity**

We've made a major investment in our future. Now comes the work of making that investment pay off.

Here are five challenges you'll help us tackle:

* **Strengthen our new manufacturing operation.** Continue ramping up our Fort Collins facility, improving production stability, quality, capacity, and efficiency.
* **Improve scheduling and throughput.** Build better production planning and workflows across manufacturing, engraving, and shipping to improve delivery performance and reduce bottlenecks.
* **Build systems that last.** Reduce dependence on individual employees by developing practical SOPs, standardized processes, clear performance measures, and repeatable operating routines.
* **Develop our next generation of leaders.** Coach newer managers, strengthen accountability, and build employee development practices that help great people grow.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Use Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and practical root-cause problem-solving to reduce waste, improve productivity, and create measurable, sustainable improvements.

You'll have meaningful ownership of these challenges, the support of our leadership team, and the freedom to make a lasting impact.

**Who We're Looking For**

We're looking for a rare combination of heart, head, and hands. Someone who can lead people, build systems, solve problems, and roll up their sleeves when the work demands it.

**What you must bring:**

* **Proven People Leadership:** Demonstrated success leading teams in a manufacturing or production environment, ideally 20 or more employees, with experience developing supervisors or managers and holding people accountable.
* **Demonstrated Systems Building:** A track record of improving processes, implementing operational improvements, and building systems that continue to work without your constant involvement.
* **High Agency & Ownership:** The judgment, initiative, work ethic, and follow-through to take responsibility for results, solve difficult problems, and lead confidently in a hands-on environment.

**What we'd love to see:**

* Experience in plastic injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience applying Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement methods. Certifications are valued but not required.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management, purchasing, and quality systems.
* Strong financial and analytical skills, with an understanding of how operational decisions affect profitability.
* Experience developing managers, building teams, and helping an organization prepare for growth.

We value experience, but we're far more interested in what you've accomplished than the number of years on your résumé.

**Seasoned plastics professionals and exceptional leaders from other manufacturing environments are equally encouraged to apply.** What matters most is demonstrated leadership, systems thinking, operational judgment, and a willingness to keep learning.

***The Ritchey Way***

Our culture is built around one simple commitment: **DO RIGHT BY THE RANCH.**

Four core principles guide how we show up every day:

**ASK WHY. ASK WHAT IF.** — Learn the work. Make it better.

**MAKE THE SMALL THINGS COUNT.** — Bring care to the details, seen or unseen.

**NO SIDELINES.** — See it. Say it. Help solve it.

**BE GOOD TO WORK WITH.** — Carry your share. Be good company.

These aren't just words on a wall. They're the standards we hold ourselves and each other to. As our Director of Operations, you'll help bring *The Ritchey Way* to life through your leadership, your example, and the team you build.

**Why Ritchey?**

We're small enough that your ideas matter, but established and ambitious enough that your work can make a lasting difference. You'll have direct access to ownership, real authority to drive improvement, and a genuine opportunity to help shape the company's future.

**We're intentionally looking for someone with the potential to grow beyond operations.**

For the right individual who demonstrates exceptional leadership, business judgment, and results, this role could become a pathway toward broader company leadership, potentially including a future President or General Manager position.

That opportunity isn't guaranteed or tied to a timetable. It will be earned through performance, trust, and demonstrated ability to lead an increasingly complex business.

Most importantly, you'll be part of a team that takes pride in showing up every day for the farmers and ranchers who feed us.

**If you're a builder at heart, believe great people deserve great leadership, and want to create something you can be genuinely proud of, we'd love to meet you.**

**Location:** Fort Collins, Colorado — Full-Time, Onsite

**Experiencing together a unique human adventure**

Animal health is key to the health of the planet. Working at Virbac means taking part in a unique human adventure in which the engagement of each individual contributes to its evolution. Encouraging internal mobility between positions and countries, offering individual development plans and building a partnership based on trust between managers and employees are as many perspectives of motivation for our teams. We also offer them a work environment conducive to exploring new territories and balancing their professional and personal lives. Finally, fostering their engagement to animal health also means listening to them and helping them to acquire new skills, preparing them for the challenges of tomorrow and encouraging them to contribute to an ever more responsible approach to our business.

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

Virbac Animal Health is seeking a Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology to join our Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) team. The Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology develops, implements, maintains, and improves robust manufacturing processes and facility infrastructure for right-first-time manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs. To plan, schedule, organize, and manage Technology Transfer Projects, CAPEX Engineering Projects, Validation, Technical Support, Alternate Raw Materials, Packaging, Life Cycle Management, and Team Leadership.

**Qualified candidates should possess the following:**

* 8 to 12+ years of Progressively responsible experience in engineering, and production management with a cGMP/FDA-regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Demonstrated track record in CAPEX project management, facility/process design, and multi-team operational leadership across multi-site or regional organizations.
* Strong expertise in managing capital and operational expense budgets.
* Proven Leadership in process improvement , life cycle management, and technology transfers.
* In-depth knowledge of cGMP, EHS regulations, and sustainable engineering practices.
* Strong multi-team leadership, communication, and cross-functional stakeholder management abilities.

**Benefits:** 13 Company paid Holidays; 5 Floating Holidays (prorated); 15 vacation days (prorated); 5 floating holidays (prorated); 6% 401k match; competitive pay and bonus opportunity; growth opportunities within the department and much more!

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

**Area of responsibility 1: Technology Transfer Activities**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the budget, planning, and robust manufacturing (RFT for the first commercial batches) of technology transfer projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Accountable for the definition and execution of the site and regional project roadmap in alignment with business needs and capability.
* Contributes to the selection of the right technology or CMO, taking into account product needs.
* Establish robust cost estimates (CAPEX, resources, future running costs) and planning estimates to support reliable NPVs and commercial strategy.
* Leadership of scale-up batches, engineering batches, and transfer to production.
* Develops manufacturing documentation (Master Batch Records, Submission batch protocols, etc.).
* Reviews and approves transfer and submission files.

**Expected results:** Ensure the robustness and capability of the process transferred to Manufacturing

**Area of responsibility 2: CAPEX Engineering Projects**

**Main activities:**

* Support and lead CAPEX engineering projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Evaluate, scope, and implement CAPEX projects for facility infrastructure, process improvements, and product needs.
* Responsible for managing annual capital budgets and operating expenses for the department.
* Partner closely with key local and global stakeholders (Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, Finance, etc.) to align project execution with regional operational goals.
* Ensure all engineering projects are performed in full compliance with applicable cGMP standards, EHS regulations, and company sustainability objectives.
* Oversee project budgets, engineering designs, contractor selection, and commissioning/qualification timelines.

**Expected Results:** Successful, on-time, and on-budget delivery of facility, process, and product CAPEX engineering projects that enhance regional capacity, EHS standards, compliance, and efficiency.

**Area of responsibility 3:** Process Improvement & Life Cycle Management (LCM)

**Main Activities:**

* Incorporate structured process improvement concepts (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) across existing product portfolios.
* Lead Life Cycle Management changes to maintain and optimize the existing commercial product portfolio across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Collaborate closely with global and local stakeholders, including Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, and Finance, to evaluate and execute LCM initiatives.

**Expected Results:** Drive continuous product and process enhancement, lower operational costs, ensure ongoing regulatory compliance, and extend product life cycles.

**Area of responsibility 4: Validation**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the generation, technical review, execution, and technical approval of validation deliverables (Validation Master Plan, URS, equipment qualification, process validation, cleaning validation, computer system validation)across NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Lead validation projects and teams
* Ensures risk analysis methods are applied to validation activities
* Follow industry and regulatory trends and expectations (GMP, EHS, and sustainability guidelines).
* Review SOPs and batch documentation to ensure adequacy with validation criteria.
* Ensure prompt deviation resolution, including root cause analysis when required.

**Expected results:** A thorough understanding of the validation status of the regional sites, products, and equipment, with proactive remediation plans addressing any gaps.

**Area of responsibility 5: Technical support.**

**Main activities:**

* Troubleshooting and improvement proposal of current commercial products processes (robustness, productivity, cost efficiency & compliance)
* Lean and methodological approach during trouble shooting of complex product/process deviations
* Take ownership of complex product deviation / CAPA until approval
* Contribute to solution design in collaboration with R&D, Quality Assurance, Regulatory, etc.
* Develop, apply and train teams on efficient troubleshooting and optimization methodologies (FMEA,root cause analysis, etc)

**Expected results:** Deliver strong technical and operational process mastery to support manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.

**Area of responsibility 6: Alternate Raw materials**

**Main activities:**

* Technical feasibility assessments and reporting.
* Leads the engineering or validation batches (protocols/reports)
* Coordinates with the other departments (e.g. Quality Control, Regulatory Affairs)to support raw material changes.

**Expected results:** Support strategic sourcing and continuity of supply through alternate raw material qualifications.

**Area of responsibility 7: Packaging**

**Main activities:**

* Leadership of the packaging change controls and CAPAs (eg: alternate packaging components)
* Collaborates with packaging suppliers on new packaging equipment/materials, and technical feasibility assessments…
* Creates packaging specifications, including drawings and written text areas. Prepares and provides cost estimates for new packaging materials.
* Initiates, leads and Implements packaging improvements for existing products to reduce costs and/or improve packaging and product quality.

**Expected results:** Lead packaging design and modifications to drive productivity, efficiency and cost reductions while maintaining all customer and regulatory requirements.

**Area of responsibility 6: Team Leadership**

**Main Activities:**

* Translate team missions into clear, actionable SMART objectives

* Evaluate team performance through key indicators and foster a Lean culture.

with Virbac values while promoting a safe, sustainable working environment.

**Expected results:** Define and implement the NORAM Engineering & MSAT vision and organizational structure in alignment with group strategy.

OPPORTUNITY

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
* Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ

External manufacturing and CDMO management

* Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
* Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
* Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
* Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
* Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
* Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
* Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
* Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
* Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets

Regulatory and cross-functional support

* Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
* Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
* Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts

Team and resource leadership

* In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
* Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
* Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation

### **REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
* 6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
* Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
* Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
* Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
* Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
* Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
* Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
* Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
* Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
* Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
* Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
* Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
* Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
* Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
* Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
* Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation
* Experience building a function or team from the ground up in a small or mid-size biotech
* Working knowledge of statistical tools for DoE and process data analysis (e.g., JMP, Minitab)

### **BENEFITS**

* Company-paid health/vision/dental benefits
* Unlimited vacation and generous sick time
* Company-sponsored meals and snacks
* Wellness, caregiver and ergonomics benefits
* 401(k) with company matching

Actual base salary will be determined by relevant professional experience, applicable skills, and internal equity

**COMPANY**

Mammoth Biosciences is a biotechnology company focused on leveraging its proprietary ultracompact CRISPR systems to develop long-term curative therapies, as well as other applications such as decentralized precision diagnostics. Founded by CRISPR pioneer and Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Trevor Martin, Janice Chen, and Lucas Harrington, the company’s ultracompact proteins are designed to enable *in vivo* gene editing in difficult to reach tissues utilizing both nuclease applications and new editing modalities beyond double stranded breaks, including base editing, gene writing, and epigenetic editing. The company is building out its pipeline of potential *in vivo* gene editing therapeutics and capabilities and has partnerships with leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to broaden the reach of its innovative and proprietary technology. Mammoth’s deep science and industry experience, along with a robust and differentiated intellectual property portfolio, have enabled the company to further its mission to transform the lives of patients and deliver on the full promise of CRISPR technologies.

**About CAMP Systems:**  
At CAMP Systems, we are the trusted leader in aircraft compliance and health management, proudly serving the global business aviation industry. With over 20,000 aircraft and 33,000 engines supported on our cutting-edge platforms, and partnerships with more than 1,300 maintenance facilities and parts suppliers worldwide, we’re shaping the future of aviation technology. Since our founding in 1968, we’ve grown to a dynamic team of 1,600+ employees across 14 locations globally—all united by a passion for innovation and excellence.

**Our Mission & Vision:**  
We connect the aviation industry through smart technology to make flight safer and more efficient, driving the future of aviation with intelligence and exceptional customer experiences.

**Our Values & Excellence Mindset:**  
We are customer obsessed, trust-driven, owners of our work, stronger together, constantly curious, and boldly innovative.

  

**What You Will Experience in This Role:**

The Director – Quality Assurance drives quality across CAMP's Aircraft Health Management business and provides quality oversight for data and process quality concerns. The role owns the QMS, the internal audit program, and the full quality escape lifecycle, and serves as CAMP's quality voice with OEMs, regulators, and key customers. The right candidate combines deep aviation maintenance knowledge with a disciplined, data-driven approach to compliance and continuous improvement.

This is a high-visibility leadership role reporting to the Vice President, Aviation Health Management Operations. The Director partners with senior leaders across a global organization and will build on an established quality program: strengthening the QMS, deepening OEM and customer confidence, and scaling quality practices as AHM grows.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategy & Leadership**

* Own and lead quality strategy across the full Aircraft Health Management organization, spanning maintenance tracking and engine health monitoring services, aligned with CAMP's business objectives.
* Serve as the escalation point for quality complaints from customer-facing, maintenance compliance, engine health monitoring, flight scheduling, and inventory functions.
* Partner with senior management and departmental leaders to embed quality methodologies across the organization and lead the associated change management.
* Own the quality budget, resource plan, and tooling (QMS, audit, and corrective action platforms), and build the succession pipeline for the quality team.

**Quality Management System & Certification**

* Own the Quality Management System (QMS) and quality SOPs, driving continuous improvement and ensuring processes meet strict regulatory and OEM requirements.

#### **Director of Pharmacy Operations, Quality & Compliance**

ProCompounding Pharmacy is seeking an experienced pharmacist to provide leadership across pharmacy operations, quality systems, regulatory compliance, and sterile and nonsterile compounding.

This is a senior, hands-on leadership position for someone who understands both the technical and operational demands of a growing 503A compounding pharmacy. The successful candidate will help strengthen our pharmacy infrastructure, develop our people, maintain regulatory readiness, and build practical systems that support quality, consistency, and continued growth.

#### **Key Responsibilities**

#### **The Director of Pharmacy Operations, Quality and Compliance will:**

* Provide leadership and oversight for pharmacy operations, quality, and regulatory compliance.
* Support sterile and nonsterile compounding operations and ensure alignment with applicable standards and regulations.
* Maintain and continuously improve the pharmacy's quality management systems.
* Oversee compliance with USP 795, 797, and 800 requirements.
* Lead preparation for regulatory inspections, accreditation surveys, and internal quality reviews.
* Manage investigations, deviations, rootcause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and related quality initiatives.
* Develop practical policies, procedures, and operating systems that improve consistency and accountability.
* Coach, develop, and support pharmacy team members and emerging leaders.
* Partner with ownership and leadership on operational priorities, risk management, and growth initiatives.
* Monitor regulatory developments and help ensure compliance across multiple states.

#### **Ideal Background**

#### **Strong candidates will bring:**

* Pharmacist licensure and significant experience within a 503A compounding pharmacy.
* Leadership experience involving pharmacy operations, quality, compliance, or staff management.
* Experience with both sterile and nonsterile compounding strongly preferred.
* Board Certification in Sterile Compounding Pharmacy (BCSCP) preferred.
* Working knowledge of USP 795, 797, and 800.
* Experience with inspections, accreditation, investigations, CAPA processes, and quality improvement.
* The ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical operating processes.
* Strong leadership, communication, documentation, and problemsolving skills.
* Experience working within a multistate pharmacy environment.

Experience in 503B outsourcing facilities, pharmaceutical manufacturing, or cGMP environments would be an additional advantage.

Multistate pharmacist licensure is not required.

#### **The Opportunity**

ProCompounding is a growing organization where senior leaders remain close to the work. This position is well suited for someone who enjoys building systems, solving problems, developing people, and taking ownership rather than operating within a highly layered corporate structure.

We are open to qualified candidates nationally and are willing to discuss relocation for the right individual. Experienced professionals who are ready to expand their leadership responsibilities are encouraged to apply.

MISSION: At ProCompounding Pharmacy, we provide personalized medications tailored to meet each individual's specific health requirements. With a commitment to excellence, integrity, and innovation, we stand at the forefront of pharmaceutical compounding, bridging the gap between traditional pharmacy and cutting-edge healthcare solutions. OUR SERVICES: We specialize in compounding services, including: \* Hormone Replacement Therapy \* Pediatric Compounding \* Veterinary Compounding \* Dermatology and Wound Care \* Pain Management \* Dental Compounding \* Over the counter supplements Each service is conducted with the highest standards, using pharmaceutical-grade ingredients and state-of-the-art compounding techniques. Our pharmacists work closely with healthcare providers to develop formulations that address our patients' precise needs.

**Position Description**
------------------------

This role represents a critical executive leadership opportunity for a dynamic Director of Operations – Chillers to join the Global Operations team. Reporting directly to the VP of Global Operations with a dotted-line relationship to the Vice President & General Manager (VPGM) of the Chillers business unit, this leader has direct operational responsibility for all global chiller manufacturing plants.

Each global chiller facility holds full SQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) execution accountability. To drive self-sufficient, world-class execution at the plant level, the Director of Operations – Chillers will lead a comprehensive, multi-functional organization where each plant team includes dedicated Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations resources.

As an integral member of the Global Operations team, this individual operates as an influential peer to Supply Chain (partnering to enable global Supply Chain and SIOP execution) and Materials (partnering to enable Materials management and Localized Procurement strategies), as well as the broader Global Operations leadership team. By bridging global functional capabilities with plant-level execution and business unit strategy, the Director of Operations – Chillers will drive rapid operational transformation, capacity expansion, and sustainable business growth.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **1. Global Plant Leadership & SQDC Execution Accountability**

* Hold direct operational oversight and P&L/conversion cost accountability for all global chiller manufacturing facilities.
* Drive rigorousSQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) daily management and execution across every chiller site:

* **Safety:** Champion a zero-injury culture, ensuring proactive EHS compliance, ergonomic improvements, and behavioral safety leadership across all plants.
* **Quality:** Ensure zero-defect manufacturing standards, robust quality management systems, customer compliance, and rapid root-cause corrective actions.
* **Delivery:** Achieve industry-leading on-time delivery (OTD) and lead-time competitiveness through effective line balancing, capacity tracking, and constraint management.
* **Cost:** Optimize direct and indirect labor productivity, overhead absorption, scrap reduction, and continuous conversion cost improvements.

### **2. Multi-Functional Team Management & Talent Development**

* Lead, mentor, and develop Plant Managers and site leadership teams across the global chiller footprint.
* Ensure each plant's respective organization is effectively structured and resourced across Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations to deliver autonomous day-to-day SQDC execution.
* Build organizational capability, establish clear succession plans, and foster an empowered, high-accountability, results-oriented culture across both salaried and direct labor workforces.

**Job Responsibilities Continued**
----------------------------------

**3. Matrixed & Peer Collaboration**

* **Business Unit Alignment (Dotted Line to VPGM of Chillers):** Serve as a strategic operational partner to the VPGM of Chillers, translating commercial growth strategies, customer requirements, and new product introductions (NPI) into scalable manufacturing execution plans.
* **Supply Chain & SIOP Partnership (Peer to Supply Chain):** Collaborate closely with Supply Chain and the Supply Chain/SIOP organization to align long-term capacity planning, master production scheduling, demand-supply balancing, and headcount/capacity models.
* **Materials & Localized Procurement Partnership (Peer to Materials):** Partner closely with Materials and the Materials/Procurement organization to optimize plant-level material flow, inventory turns, working capital, supplier quality/delivery performance, and localized sourcing strategies.
* **Global Operations Synergy:** Collaborate with fellow peers on the Global Operations leadership team to standardize best practices, leverage shared subassembly/hub strategies, and drive enterprise-wide operational initiatives.

### **4. Operational Excellence, Footprint Strategy & Continuous Improvement**

* Define and execute the end-to-end global manufacturing strategy for the Chillers business, aligning footprint optimization, capital investments (CapEx), and automation roadmaps with long-term growth targets.
* Embed Lean manufacturing principles, 80/20 simplification, value-stream mapping, and continuous improvement methodologies across all global chiller sites.
* Support modular design integration, subassembly standardization, and agile manufacturing practices in partnership with Advanced Manufacturing Engineering and Design Engineering.

**Required Education & Qualifications**
---------------------------------------

* **Bachelor’s degree** in Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related technical discipline is required.
* **10+ years** of progressive experience in manufacturing and operations leadership roles (e.g., Plant Manager, Senior Operations Manager, Director of Operations) within complex, engineered-to-order or configure-to-order industrial/HVAC manufacturing environments.
* **5+ years** of proven experience leading multi-site / global manufacturing operations, demonstrating measurable improvements in SQDC metrics.
* Demonstrated success leading cross-functional plant organizations encompassing Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations.
* Deep functional knowledge of Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, 80/20 principles, Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP), material replenishment systems, and localized procurement interfaces.
* Proven ability to thrive in a matrixed organizational structure, effectively balancing solid-line functional excellence (to the VP, Global Operations) with dotted-line commercial business unit alignment (to the VPGM of Chillers).
* Exceptional executive presence, communication, and interpersonal influencing skills, with a collaborative approach to working with peer leaders across Supply Chain, Materials, Engineering, and Finance.
* Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally (up to 30%–50% depending on home base location) to support global chiller manufacturing plants.

**Why Choose Modexus Solutions?**

protected_roles.description:
*Join the world's largest HVAC company!*
Daikin Applied is seeking a
**Director of Operations.**
You will have the ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth. The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best. Come be a part of an exciting journey at Daikin Applied, where innovation and excellence drive our every endeavor!
  
  
**Location:**
Staunton, VA– onsite
  
  
**Your Responsibilities**

* Develops and maintains manufacturing operations business plans to include all program requirements, labor hours, production costs, backlogs, quality and other related manufacturing statistics.
* Provides input to the development of product strategy and research and development of new and emerging products.
* Establishes production and quality control standards, develops budget and cost controls, and obtains data regarding types, quantities, specifications, and delivery dates of products ordered.
* Provides guidance to the development of a manufacturing process plan, including personnel requirements, material needs, subcontract requirements, facility needs, and tooling and equipment needs.
* Ensures all established costs, quality, and delivery commitments are met.
* Coordinates manufacturing activities with all other functions of the organization and suppliers to obtain optimum production and utilization of human resources, machines, and equipment.
* Reviews production, operating and financial reports and communicates information to executive management.
* Determines responsibilities of assigned organization and staff positions to accomplish business objectives.
* Develops plant policies and supervises the application of such policies. Ensures that all assigned employees are aware of and comply with company, government, and customer policies, procedures, and regulations.
* Participates in organizational development to ensure appropriate and adequate utilization of labor, machinery and equipment. Takes action to implement changes/improvements when necessary.
* Oversees the implementation of manufacturing schedules based on sales requirements and plant capacity.
* Monitors production activities to eliminate delays and ensure adherence to production and shopping schedules.
* Maintains effective communications with Engineering, Purchasing, Materials, Customer Service, Marketing and other departments to constantly seek production improvements, minimize costs and ensure maximum customer satisfaction.
* Oversees a strong, proactive safety program to promote a safe, healthy working environment for all plant employees.
* Seeks to maintain a mutually beneficial relationship with the union and provides information in periodic Labor-Management meetings.
* Maintains conformance to budgetary limitations in all departments.
* Manages supervisors and other employees by establishing goals, allocating resources, assessing annual performance and determining individual merit and promotional increases.

**Your Qualifications**

* 4-year bachelor’s degree in a related field
* 10 years of related experience
* 6+ years of people leading experience

**Your Benefits**
Daikin Applied offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements:
  
  

* Multiple medical insurance plan options + dental and vision insurance
* 401K retirement plan with employer match
* Paid time off and company paid holidays
* Paid sick time in accordance with the federal, state and local law
* Tuition Reimbursement after 6 months of continuous service

Work visa sponsorship is not available for this position
  
  
The typical annual base salary for this position ranges from $142,600 to $250,900 + bonus incentive program eligibility up to 30% in Virginia. The range displayed represents the pay range for all positions in the job grade which this position falls. Individual base pay will depend on a wide range of factors including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.
  
  
Employment is contingent upon successful completion of pre-employment requirements, including verification of employment history, education, background screening, and drug testing where permitted by law. Safety-sensitive positions may require cannabis (marijuana) testing. All testing and employment decisions will comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws.
  
  
If you're looking for an engaging career with growth opportunities in a supportive environment, you'll love a career at Daikin Applied!

**Job Summary**
**JOB DESCRIPTION**
The Director of Manufacturing Operations provides hands-on operational leadership for the Delaware manufacturing site. The role is accountable for safe, reliable, and cost-effective execution of the production plan; disciplined planning and scheduling; WIP flow; productivity and yield improvement; operational quality; maintenance and facilities coordination; and development of a high-performing Operations organization. The Director works across the business to translate customer and strategic requirements into executable operating plans and measurable results.
  
  
The Director is expected to build strong working relationships with Engineering, Quality, EHS, Purchasing, Finance, Supply Chain, Human Resources, Sales, and Product Management and lead through influence where responsibilities cross functional boundaries.
  
  
**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**
Operational Leadership
  
  

* Lead daily manufacturing execution across the Delaware site, maintaining a visible and hands-on presence with employees and leaders at all levels.
* Direct and develop the Production Manager, Planner/Scheduler, Maintenance Manager, and Special Projects Manager. The Production Manager leads three Shift Supervisors.
* Set clear operating expectations, establish performance routines, remove barriers, and hold leaders accountable for results and behaviors.
* Maintain focus on the highest-value priorities while resisting a crisis-driven operating model.
* Coordinate with Engineering, Quality, EHS, Purchasing, Finance, Supply Chain, Human Resources, Sales, and Product Management to resolve issues and execute site priorities.

Planning Scheduling and Flow
  
  

* Establish and maintain a reliable planning and scheduling process aligned with customer commitments, available capacity, material availability, staffing, and equipment constraints.
* Improve visibility and control of WIP, production flow, supermarkets, constraints, and recovery plans through the Planner/Scheduler and operating reviews.
* Use data to identify bottlenecks, improve throughput, reduce lead time, and support fact-based decisions on priorities and resources.
* Partner with Purchasing and Supply Chain to ensure material availability supports the production plan without creating unnecessary inventory or disruption.

Quality Safety and Continuous Improvement
  
  

* Own operational quality performance by building quality into processes, reinforcing standards, and ensuring timely containment and effective corrective action.
* Partner with Quality to maintain applicable certifications and management systems, prepare for audits, and strengthen process discipline and change control.
* Lead a culture in which employees identify problems, escalate concerns early, follow standard work, and take ownership of the process and outcome.
* Lead Lean and continuous-improvement activity that produces measurable gains in productivity, yield, quality, cost, delivery, and flow.
* Partner with EHS to establish safe work practices, address hazards, reinforce accountability, and achieve strong site safety performance.

People Labor and Culture
  
  

* Build a high-performing Operations team through selection, onboarding, coaching, development, recognition, and fair, consistent performance management.
* Develop and coach supervisors and other leaders to manage through facts, engage employees, and sustain improvements across shifts.
* Maintain a constructive day-to-day relationship with the Teamsters workforce and support Human Resources in contract administration, grievances, and future negotiations.
* Promote the company values of Integrity, Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, and Enthusiasm through personal example and consistent leadership.

Financial Capital and Customer Support
  
  

* Manage Operations performance and cost control within the budget established by the GM, using data to identify savings opportunities and improve labor, material, equipment, and operating effectiveness.
* Develop the initial site capital plan and business cases for automation and other investments. Drive approved projects to completion on schedule and within budget.
* Support Sales as the primary operational partner for customer escalations, visits, delivery discussions, and technical or manufacturing topics. Sales remains the primary customer interface.
* Provide concise, timely, and fact-based operating updates to the Sr. Director of Global Operations and leadership team.

**Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering required; Mechanical or Chemical Engineering preferred.
* At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing or operations leadership.
* Required: demonstrated Lean leadership and continuous-improvement results in productivity, yield, quality, cost, delivery, or flow.
* Required: experience establishing or improving production planning, scheduling, WIP control, and shop-floor flow.
* Preferred: experience managing a unionized workforce.
* Preferred: experience in advanced materials, ceramics, semiconductor components, precision fabrication, or other complex industrial manufacturing.
* Preferred: experience implementing or significantly improving an ERP or manufacturing execution system.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through others, develop teams, resolve problems, and sustain accountability in a changing environment.

**Skills**

* Hands-on, visible, and self-motivated leadership style with a strong sense of urgency and ownership.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and fact-based decision-making skills.
* Ability to establish priorities, execute with discipline, and convert strategy into practical operating routines.
* Ability to influence across functions and the organization and work effectively with technical, commercial, and corporate partners.
* Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, and presentation skills.
* Ability to work effectively with employees and leaders across shifts and levels of the organization.
* Due to ITAR compliance, this position requires candidates to be a U.S. Citizen, Permanent Resident Alien, or Protected Individual per 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

**Working Conditions**
Regular work in a manufacturing environment is expected, including time on the production floor. The position requires the ability to sit, stand, bend, squat, and walk throughout the facility and to occasionally lift, push, or pull up to 10 pounds. Up to 20% domestic and international travel may be required as business needs dictate.
  
  
**Safety Requirements**
All employees are required to follow the site EHS procedures and Coherent Corp. Corporate EHS standards.
  
  
**Quality And Environmental Responsibilities**
Depending on location, this position may be responsible for the execution and maintenance of the ISO 9000, 9001, 14001 and/or other applicable standards that may apply to the relevant roles and responsibilities within the Quality Management System and Environmental Management System.
  
  
**Culture Commitment**
Ensure adherence to company’s values (ICARE) in all aspects of your position at Coherent Corp.:
  
  
**I**
ntegrity – Create an Environment of Trust
  
  
**C**
ollaboration – Innovate Through the Sharing of Ideas
  
  
**A**
ccountability – Own the Process and the Outcome
  
  
**R**
espect – Recognize the Value in Everyone
  
  
**E**
nthusiasm – Find a Sense of Purpose in Work
  
  
*Coherent Corp. is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.*
*If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at*
*talentacquisition@coherent.com*
*.*
**About Us**
Coherent is a global leader in lasers, engineered materials and networking components. We are a vertically integrated manufacturing company that develops innovative products for diversified applications in the industrial, optical communications, military, life sciences, semiconductor equipment, and consumer markets. Coherent provides a comprehensive career development platform within an environment that challenges employees to perform at their best, while rewarding excellence and hard-work through a competitive compensation program. It's an exciting opportunity to work for a company that offers stability, longevity and growth. Come Join Us!

We will not pay for unsolicited resumes from recruiters and employment agencies unless we have a signed agreement and have required assistance, in writing, for a specific opening.

**Job Description**
**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.
  
  
**Essential Responsibilities**
**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

**Good Manufacturing & Documentation Practices**
Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.
  
  

* Perform all documentation in compliance with ALCOA++ principles and site SOPs.
* Adhere to applicable cGMP documents including SOPs, batch records, protocols, change controls, and controlled forms.
* Keep all required cGMP training current and escalate quality concerns along with proposed solutions to the Quality department.

**Qualifications**
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
* Minimum 5–10 years of mid to senior management experience in a manufacturing or process environment
* Demonstrated understanding of the responsibilities and functions of key departments within a pharmaceutical or industrial manufacturing facility
* Strong knowledge of cGMP compliance, technical operations, and quality systems within a manufacturing environment
* Proven ability to identify, develop, and inspire leaders at multiple levels of the organization
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to present strategy and performance clearly to site and functional leadership

**Preferred**

* Experience with API development and manufacturing processes
* Certification in Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma

**Physical Requirements**
The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear.
* Frequently required to use hands to handle or feel objects, reach with hands and arms, and climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**
The work environment characteristics described below are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regular work in a standard office environment, with frequent entry into the production area of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility.
* Production environment may include moving mechanical parts, fumes or airborne particles, extreme heat, wet or humid conditions, low levels of toxic or caustic chemicals, and outdoor weather conditions.
* Noise level in the work environment is typically moderate.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. ****Panther: Better Health Is Skin Deep****
Panther is building the leading skin-powered treatment delivery and data platform for health and longevity. Its proprietary intradermal SmartPatch™ precisely delivers treatments to activate local and systemic healing, unlocking the skin as a scalable gateway for care. Panther’s AI-based platform accelerates partners’ product development and personalizes treatment, resulting in compelling consumer and provider experiences. Panther is targeting economically attractive markets of increasing clinical and regulatory difficulty, starting with its PIQUE™ branded Skincare products in mid-2027, and rapidly progressing to Medical Aesthetics and Therapeutics thereafter. Panther’s platform, significant IP portfolio and staged regulatory strategy provide a defensible moat. Panther is led by a team of successful entrepreneurs and operators and is advised by leading scientific experts.
  
  
**The Opportunity**
Panther Life Sciences is building a new category of consumer-centric health and beauty products powered by our SmartPatch platform. As we move from development into commercialization, manufacturing becomes the critical unlock for scale, quality, and customer trust.
  
  
We are seeking a Director of Manufacturing Operations to own this transition end-to-end. This role is responsible for translating innovative R&D into reliable, high-quality, and scalable commercial production across both cosmetic and medical device products. You will lead the build-out of Panther's manufacturing strategy, serving as the bridge between internal development teams and external CMO partners.
  
  
You will define how manufacturing operates at Panther, from selecting and standing up partners, to leading technology transfer, to building the systems that allow us to scale from thousands to millions of units. This is not a maintenance role. You will be building the manufacturing function from scratch. Your work will directly impact product availability, customer experience, and the company's ability to grow.
  
  
You will work closely with the leadership team and cross-functional team members in formulation, device development, and quality to establish a manufacturing engine that supports both near-term commercial goals and long-term platform expansion. This is for someone who wants to build, scale, and set the standard for manufacturing in a category-defining company with a great team and a platform that is already generating clinical results. If you want to build something that matters, we want to hear from you.
  
  
Some travel will required approximately 10% -30%
  
  
This role is ideally based in Pittsburgh, with New York as an alternative location."
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**CDMO & Manufacturing Operations**

* Serve as the primary relationship owner and day-to-day point of contact for CMO partners
* Lead technology transfer from R&D to clinical and commercial manufacturing
* Oversee late-stage clinical and commercial production across product lines
* Drive manufacturing performance metrics including yield, throughput, and product quality
* Support CMO selection and onboarding, including process validation and scale-up
* Build and manage supply chain, logistics, fulfillment, and inventory operations
* Own material sourcing and supplier relationships
* Identify critical dependencies and build supplier redundancy to mitigate risk

**Scaling, Systems & Financial Planning**

* Build the manufacturing line from the ground up with a path from ~10K to ~1M units per month
* Drive automation, process optimization, and line redesign as production scales
* Own manufacturing cost modeling and financial planning (FP&A) for operations
* Develop sourcing strategy and budget frameworks in partnership with finance and leadership
* Establish systems and processes to support future team growth and internal manufacturing capabilities

**Quality, Compliance & Cross-Functional Leadership**

* Ensure manufacturing quality, regulatory compliance, and adherence to QMS
* Partner cross-functionally with leadership, formulation, device, and quality teams
* Contribute to customer satisfaction through reliable product delivery and issue resolution

**Qualifications**

* Proven experience scaling a product from R&D to commercial manufacturing in a regulated environment
* Experience overseeing manufacturing operations for a Class II or III medical device or equivalent regulated product
* Hands-on experience scaling production volumes significantly (e.g., 10x or more)
* Direct experience working with CMO partners including selection, onboarding, and tech transfer
* Experience managing supply chain, logistics, inventory, and fulfillment operations
* Familiarity with Quality Management Systems (QMS) in regulated environments
* Demonstrated ability to lead technology transfer and process scale-up
* Experience with manufacturing cost modeling and financial planning
* Direct people management experience

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with combination products (drug + device), such as auto-injectors, EpiPens, nasal sprays, or microarray-based systems
* Background in Material Science & Technology Transfer (MSNT)
* Experience scaling production to high-volume output (100K+ units per month)
* Experience across both cosmetic and medical device products
* Experience with automation and line redesign in a manufacturing scale-up context
* Background in customer support or customer-facing operations within manufacturing
* Experience managing managers or building multi-layered organizations
* Strong systems orientation with experience implementing or optimizing operational infrastructure

**Benefits**

* Build something unique and high-impact with a world-class team of experts in technology, healthcare, and science.
* Equity in the form of stock options
* Competitive health insurance, including 90% employer-paid medical, plus dental and vision
* Life, AD&D and short-term disability insurance
* Paid time off and paid company holidays
* In-person company events
* Fully stocked kitchen

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
Panther Life Sciences is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital or partnership status, age, national origin, citizenship, veteran or military status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, caregiver status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

You will advance a safer, more reliable, and more resilient electrical grid. Our products help the grid adapt to severe weather and transition to clean energy. We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively.
  
  
Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner

**Compensation**
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices.

Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
  
  
**Join Our Team as a Senior Manager - Supplier Quality**
!
  
  
The Senior Manager - Supplier Quality is responsible for ensuring that all suppliers meet or exceed the company’s quality standards through strategic audits, risk mitigation, and continuous supplier development. This role emphasizes proactive engagement with suppliers to ensure compliance, minimize risks, and ultimately ensure the quality of supplied components to S&C. The position also oversees the qualification and ongoing evaluation of suppliers to align with the company’s operational and commercial objectives.
  
  
**Essential Functions**

* Supplier Audits & Qualification: Formulate and implement a comprehensive operational strategy to drive continuous quality improvement initiatives within the supplier quality function. Lead a team that conducts comprehensive audits and supplier qualification processes, ensuring compliance with quality standards and the prevention of defective component shipments from the supplier to S&C. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to assess supplier capabilities and align with company requirements.
* COPQ: Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Take ownership of reducing the cost of poor quality (COPQ) by analyzing trends in supplier-reported issues, identifying root causes, and implementing preventative measures to ensure continuous improvement in product quality.
* Production Part Approval Process (PPAP): Oversee the PPAP process to validate supplier-provided components meet specified requirements. Ensure that documentation, testing, and approvals are conducted thoroughly and accurately.
* Risk Analysis and Mitigation: Perform supplier risk analysis by evaluating historical performance, process controls, and financial stability. Develop and execute mitigation strategies to minimize potential supply chain disruptions.
* Corrective Action and Accountability: Lead the resolution of supplier-related quality issues through effective corrective action processes. Establish clear accountability frameworks to ensure sustained improvements and proactive prevention of non-confirming/defective components before receiving them.
* Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as a subject matter expert in Supplier Quality, staying abreast of industry best practices, standards, and technological advancements and ensuring the greater quality function is well-versed in the latest quality methodologies and tools, facilitating a high level of technical proficiency.
* Continuous Improvement: Analyze quality feedback and metrics to identify trends and improvement opportunities. Set team targets for various KPIs and collaborate with production groups to recommend quality targets. Implement a data-driven decision-making process to enhance overall product quality and operational efficiency.
* QA System Support: Manage the meticulous documentation of quality processes, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and internal and external compliance requirements. Provide strategic guidance for regular review and updates, incorporating changes in processes, standards, and best practices to maintain a compliant and dynamic quality management system.
* Functional Leadership: Provide strong leadership and direction to managers and senior contributors, setting clear performance expectations, and fostering a culture of accountability and excellence. Conduct regular performance assessments, provide constructive feedback, and facilitate career development opportunities to support individual growth and organizational succession planning.
* Thought Leadership: Provide thought leadership and best-practice direction to the quality assurance team, ensuring the execution of quality goals that contribute towards the larger goals of S&C.
* Compliance: Understand and comply with all applicable content standards, brand guidelines, company policies, and rules.

**Required**
**Core Leadership & Management**

* 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in Supplier Quality, Quality Engineering, or related manufacturing quality roles.
* 5+ years in leadership or senior management roles overseeing global suppliers and multi-site operations.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical field; advanced degree or Six Sigma Black Belt preferred Preferred
* Experience in a large (2+ billion-dollar revenue) B2B manufacturing company.
* Proven ability to lead and develop a global Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) team, setting strategic direction, driving accountability, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
* Strong executive presence with the capability to influence cross‑functional leaders in engineering, operations, procurement, and manufacturing.
* Demonstrated track record of managing complex supplier ecosystems and driving measurable improvements in quality performance.
* Technical & Quality Expertise
* Deep expertise in advanced quality tools and methodologies, including APQP, PPAP, FMEA, MSA, SPC, 8D, and root-cause/containment fundamentals.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing process controls, capability studies, product validation, and statistical quality management.
* Ability to assess supplier technical capability and process maturity through detailed audits and data-driven evaluation Supplier Management & Performance Improvement
* Experience developing and deploying supplier quality strategies to ensure robust selection, onboarding, and ongoing performance monitoring.
* Proven ability to drive corrective action and continuous improvement using structured problem-solving techniques.
* Hands-on experience establishing supplier scorecards, performance targets, and escalation management processes. Operational Excellence & Risk Management
* Strong capability in managing supplier risk, including process risk assessments, qualification reviews, and proactive risk mitigation planning.
* Demonstrated experience improving cost, quality, and delivery through Lean/Six Sigma methodologies.
